h1: Buyer’s Guide: Best Gutter Installers in Salt Lake City
author: M&M Gutters & Exteriors
content:
Your Complete Guide to Gutter Installation in Salt Lake City

Gutter installation Salt Lake City homeowners need depends on understanding local climate challenges, choosing the right materials, and selecting an experienced contractor. Here’s what you need to know:

Key Considerations for Salt Lake City Gutter Installation:

  1. Materials: Aluminum (most popular), steel (heavy snow), or copper (premium durability)
  2. Style: Seamless gutters reduce leaks and improve curb appeal
  3. Size: 5-inch for standard homes, 6-inch for steep roofs or large homes
  4. Protection: Gutter guards help manage debris from cottonwoods and maples
  5. Installation Time: Most projects complete in one day
  6. Cost Factors: Home size, roof complexity, material choice, and gutter guards

Salt Lake City’s unique climate makes quality gutters essential. With over 60 inches of annual snowfall, rapid spring snowmelt from the Wasatch Mountains, and summer thunderstorms, your home faces significant water management challenges year-round. Without proper gutters, you risk foundation damage (costing $2,000-$7,500 to repair), basement flooding, siding deterioration, and landscape erosion.

The difference between functional and failing gutters can mean thousands in avoided repairs. A properly installed gutter system channels hundreds of gallons of water away from your foundation during even modest rainstorms—just 0.25 inches of rain on a 2,000 square foot home equals 312 gallons of water that needs directing away from your foundation.

I’m Nathan Nuttall at M&M Gutters & Exteriors, where we’ve specialized in gutter installation Salt Lake City homeowners trust for over 30 years. Our team understands the specific demands Utah’s climate places on gutter systems and delivers expert craftsmanship backed by industry-leading warranties.

Why a Quality Gutter System is Non-Negotiable in Utah

Gutters are the unsung heroes of your home’s exterior. In Utah, with our heavy snows and sudden downpours, a robust gutter system isn’t an accessory—it’s a necessity for protecting your most significant investment.

Without proper gutters, rainwater and snowmelt cause a cascade of costly problems. Water pools around your foundation, saturating the soil and leading to cracks that can cost $2,000-$7,500 to repair. This is a major water damage risk, especially in Utah’s clay-rich soil. Unchecked water also damages siding, leads to basement flooding, and causes landscaping erosion. This can result in rot, mold growth, and washed-out gardens.

A quality gutter system is your first line of defense, efficiently collecting and diverting water away from these vulnerable areas. It ensures that water is managed proactively, protecting your home from the top down.

Salt Lake City’s Unique Climate Challenges

Salt Lake City, along with Utah, Summit, Tooele, Davis, and Weber Counties, faces unique weather that makes effective gutters vital. We contend with a full spectrum of precipitation.

Our region’s heavy snowfall, averaging over 60 inches annually in Salt Lake City, and rapid spring snowmelt can overwhelm inadequate gutters, causing overflows and destructive ice dams. Ice dams force water under shingles, leading to leaks in your roof, attic, and interior walls.

Summer thunderstorms bring intense downpours, requiring high-capacity gutters. Frequent freeze-thaw cycles stress materials, while fall debris from cottonwood and maple trees can clog unprotected systems, rendering them useless.

Signs Your Salt Lake City Home Needs New Gutters

Your home’s gutters work hard, often out of sight, out of mind, until a problem arises. But paying attention to certain warning signs can save you a lot of headache and expense. Here are the tell-tale indicators that your Salt Lake City home might be shouting for new gutters:

  • Cracks and Splits: Any visible cracks, holes, or splits allow water to escape, defeating the gutter’s purpose.
  • Sagging or Pulling Away: Gutters sagging or pulling away from the house signal failing fasteners or the weight of debris and ice.
  • Peeling Paint: Peeling paint on or near your fascia is often caused by overflowing or leaking gutters.
  • Water Stains on Siding: Water stains or streaks on siding below the gutters are a clear sign of overflow.
  • Mildew Near Foundation: Mildew or mold near the foundation or in your basement points to excess moisture from faulty gutters.
  • Pooling Water: Puddles near your foundation or eroded landscaping after rain indicate your gutters are failing.
  • Rust Spots: For metal gutters, rust is a sign of corrosion that will lead to holes and leaks.

We recommend inspecting your gutters 2-3 times yearly, especially after the fall leaf drop and during the spring snowmelt season. Being proactive can help you catch these issues before they escalate into major problems. You can learn more about these indicators in our article, 5 Signs Your Home Needs a New Gutter System.

Choosing the Right Gutter System for Your Home

Choosing the right gutter system for your Salt Lake City home means balancing durability, performance, and aesthetics. As local experts, we help you select the best option for your home’s architecture and our climate.

Every home is unique, so we focus on custom solutions that match your roof pitch, foliage, and style. As a one-stop shop for exteriors, we use 3D visualization with HOVER technology to create accurate, customizable models from smartphone photos. This lets you see and approve the design before we start. For more insights on choosing the right system, check out Which Kind of Rain Gutter is Best for You and Your Home?.

Gutter Materials: Pros and Cons for the Wasatch Front

When it comes to gutter installation Salt Lake City, the material you choose is crucial for standing up to Utah’s demanding weather. We work with several high-quality options, each with its own advantages:

MaterialPros for Utah ClimateConsMaintenanceLifespan
AluminumMost popular, strong, rust-proof, lightweight, handles temperature fluctuations well, wide range of colors with Sherwin Williams Plastilure coating.Can dent if hit hard (e.g., by ladders).Low20+ years
SteelSuperior strength for heavy snowfall and ice, resistant to dents and warping.Heavier, typically needs a rust-resistant coating, can rust if coating is compromised.Moderate20+ years
CopperExceptional durability, forms a protective patina over time, very long-lasting, neat aesthetic.Highest initial cost, requires specialized installation.Very Low50-100 years
VinylInexpensive, DIY-friendly (sectional), lightweight.Less durable in extreme cold/heat, prone to cracking/fading, not ideal for heavy snow loads.Low10-20 years
  • Aluminum Gutters: Our most popular choice. We use heavy-gauge 0.032″ aluminum with a durable Sherwin Williams coating. It’s rust-proof, lightweight, and comes in many colors to match your home.
  • Steel Gutters: An excellent option for maximum strength against heavy snow and ice. Steel is more resistant to dents and warping than aluminum.
  • Copper Gutters: A premium, long-lasting option with best curb appeal. Copper develops a beautiful patina and can last for over 50 years, making it a worthwhile long-term investment.
  • Vinyl Gutters: We generally advise against vinyl in Utah’s climate, as it can crack and become brittle in our extreme temperatures and UV exposure. For a comprehensive comparison, see our article on Vinyl vs Aluminum Gutters: Which One Is Best?. For a general guide on materials, refer to our Rain Gutter Materials Guide.

Seamless vs. Sectional Gutters

When considering gutter installation Salt Lake City, one of the most critical decisions is between seamless and traditional sectional gutters. We firmly believe in the superiority of seamless systems, and here’s why:

  • Fewer Leaks: Sectional gutters have seams that fail and leak over time. Seamless gutters are custom-formed into a single continuous piece on-site, virtually eliminating weak points and leaks.
  • Custom Fit: We fabricate seamless gutters on-site to the exact dimensions of your roofline, ensuring a perfect fit that improves both function and appearance.
  • Improved Curb Appeal: The absence of seams provides a clean, smooth, and professional look that improves your home’s exterior.
  • Low Maintenance: With no seams to catch debris, water flows freely. This reduces the chance of clogs and the need for frequent cleaning.

You can dig deeper into the benefits of this modern approach by reading our blog, What are Seamless Rain Gutters?.

Gutter Guards: Are They Worth It in Salt Lake City?

Are gutter guards necessary in Salt Lake City? Yes. With our cottonwood and maple trees, debris is a constant issue. Gutter guards are an invaluable addition to any gutter installation Salt Lake City home.

  • Debris Prevention: Guards keep leaves, pine needles, and other debris out of your gutters, preventing the dense clogs common in our area.
  • Reduced Maintenance: You’ll spend far less time on a ladder cleaning your gutters, reducing a tedious and risky chore.
  • Clog Prevention: By keeping gutters clear, guards ensure water flows freely away from your home, preventing overflows and water damage.
  • Ice Dam Mitigation: By keeping water flowing, guards help reduce the conditions that lead to ice dams.

Investing in quality gutter guards is a proactive step towards a truly low-maintenance and highly effective gutter system. To understand more about their value, check out Leaf Guards 101 and Is a leaf guard worth it?.

Why Custom Gutter Installation in Salt Lake City is a Smart Investment

For homeowners in our area, custom gutters are a smart investment for several compelling reasons:

  • Architectural Integration: We can tailor the style, material, and color of custom gutters to perfectly complement your home’s unique architecture, from historic to modern.
  • Perfect Fit for Complex Rooflines: A custom installation ensures a perfect fit for intricate rooflines with multiple gables and pitches, guaranteeing optimal performance.
  • Improved Durability: A system designed for your home’s specific needs—with stronger mounting and proper sizing—is inherently more durable against Utah’s weather.
  • Improved Home Value: A high-performing custom gutter system protects your home from damage and boosts curb appeal, both of which increase your property’s value.

At M&M Gutters & Exteriors, we specialize in providing custom solutions that meet the specific needs of your home. Learn more about our approach to Rain Gutters Installation.

The Professional Gutter Installation Salt Lake City Process: What to Expect

When you choose M&M Gutters & Exteriors for your gutter installation Salt Lake City project, you’re investing in a streamlined, professional process. We keep you informed every step of the way.

Our process typically follows these key steps:

  1. Consultation: It all starts with a conversation. We’ll listen to your goals, assess your current gutter situation, and discuss your aesthetic preferences. This is where our 3D visualization using HOVER technology comes in handy, allowing you to see how different gutter styles and colors will look on your home before any work begins.
  2. Measurement: Our team takes precise measurements of your roofline, pitch, and overhang. Accuracy here is paramount to ensure a perfect fit and optimal water flow.
  3. Fabrication: For seamless gutters, we bring our specialized equipment directly to your site. This allows us to custom-fabricate continuous lengths of gutter that perfectly match your home’s dimensions, eliminating seams and weak points.
  4. Installation: Our experienced crew then carefully installs the new gutters, ensuring proper pitch for drainage, secure fastening to your fascia, and correct downspout placement. Safety is always our top priority, and our team uses appropriate safety equipment throughout the installation. If you have old gutters, we’ll carefully remove and dispose of them as part of our comprehensive service.
  5. Final Inspection: Once installation is complete, we conduct a thorough final inspection with you. We’ll walk you through the new system, ensure everything meets our high standards, and confirm your complete satisfaction.

Key Factors for Your Gutter Installation in Salt Lake City

Several elements come into play when planning your gutter installation Salt Lake City:

  • Home Size: Larger homes naturally require more linear feet of gutters and downspouts, impacting both material needs and installation time.
  • Roof Pitch: Steep roof pitches can generate faster water runoff, which might necessitate larger gutters or more downspouts to handle the volume effectively.
  • Gutter Size (5-inch vs 6-inch): While 5-inch gutters are standard, we often recommend 6-inch gutters for larger homes or steep roofs. They carry 20% more water, providing superior capacity for heavy rain and snowmelt.
  • Downspout Placement: Strategic placement is crucial. We often recommend larger 3×4 downspouts (40% more capacity) with extensions to carry water at least 4-10 feet from your foundation.
  • Project Timeline: Most professional gutter installations are completed within a single day. However, complex rooflines, extensive custom work, or adverse weather conditions may extend the timeline.

For a general idea of costs, you can explore our article, What is the average cost of rain gutters?.

The Importance of Professional Installation

While the idea of a DIY project can be tempting, gutter installation Salt Lake City is a job best left to the professionals, especially in our challenging climate. Here’s why:

  • Proper Slope: Professionals ensure the precise slope needed for drainage, preventing standing water and clogs—a common DIY error.
  • Secure Fastening: We securely attach gutters to withstand heavy snow and ice, preventing sagging and damage to your home.
  • Avoiding Fascia Damage: Professional installation prevents costly damage to your fascia and soffit.
  • Safety: Our trained crews have the proper equipment and safety protocols to work on ladders and roofs, avoiding the risks of a DIY project.
  • Expertise in Local Conditions: We design systems specifically to handle Salt Lake City’s heavy snow, rapid runoff, and thunderstorms.

Trying to save a few dollars with a DIY approach can often lead to costly mistakes down the road. Our articles, Why you shouldnt install your rain gutters yourself and Common Gutter Installation Mistakes, highlight the pitfalls of amateur installation.

How to Choose the Best Gutter Contractor in Salt Lake City

Choosing the right partner for your gutter installation Salt Lake City is as important as choosing the right gutter system itself. You want a company you can trust to deliver quality, durability, and peace of mind. Here’s what to look for:

  • Experience: A proven track record is key. We bring over 30 years of experience to every project, so we know how to handle Utah’s climate challenges.
  • Licensing and Insurance: A licensed and insured contractor protects you from liability for accidents or property damage.
  • Local Reviews and Reputation: Check online reviews from local homeowners. We’re proud of our strong reputation for customer satisfaction.
  • Portfolios and References: A reputable contractor should be able to show you examples of their work. We invite you to explore Our Work to see the quality we deliver.
  • Written Estimates: Insist on a detailed, written estimate outlining all work, materials, and costs. Avoid vague quotes.
  • Technology Integration: We use HOVER technology to create accurate 3D models of your home, allowing you to visualize the final result before we begin.

When researching contractors, you can also check resources like the Better Business Bureau to find reliable, A+ rated companies.

Questions to Ask Before You Hire

Before committing to a contractor for your gutter installation Salt Lake City, arm yourself with these essential questions:

  • What warranty do you offer on your gutter installations? We offer a comprehensive lifetime transferable warranty covering both materials and workmanship for peace of mind.
  • What materials do you use, and why are they best for our climate? We use premium materials like heavy-gauge aluminum, steel, and copper, and we’ll explain which is best for your home and our climate.
  • What is the experience level of your crew? Our installation team has decades of combined experience, ensuring expert craftsmanship.
  • What is the typical project timeline? Most installations are completed within a single day, depending on the complexity of your home. We’ll provide a clear timeline during your consultation.
  • How do you handle cleanup and disposal of old gutters? We handle the complete removal and disposal of your old gutters, leaving your property clean.

You can learn more about our company and our commitment to quality on our About M&M Gutters & Exteriors page.

Frequently Asked Questions about Gutter Installation

How long do rain gutters last in Utah’s climate?

The lifespan of your gutters depends on the material, installation quality, and maintenance.

  • Aluminum gutters typically last 20+ years. With proper care and regular cleaning, they can often exceed this.
  • Steel gutters also have a lifespan of 20+ years, but their longevity depends heavily on the integrity of their rust-resistant coating.
  • Copper gutters are the champions of durability, often lasting 50-100 years with proper care and maintenance. Their natural resistance to corrosion makes them incredibly resilient.

Proper maintenance is key to maximizing the lifespan of any gutter material. You can find more details in our article, How long do rain gutters last?.

How do I choose the right gutter size for my home?

Choosing the right gutter size is crucial for handling Salt Lake City’s precipitation. We consider:

  • Roof Square Footage: The larger your roof, the more water it collects.
  • Roof Pitch: A steeper roof pitch means water flows off faster and with greater force, requiring a larger capacity gutter.
  • Local Rainfall Intensity: While Salt Lake City isn’t a rainforest, we do experience intense summer thunderstorms and significant snowmelt.
  • 5-inch gutters are sufficient for most average-sized homes.
  • 6-inch gutters are recommended for larger homes, steep roofs, or areas with heavy rain and snowmelt, as they provide greater capacity.

We’ll assess your home’s specific needs during our consultation to recommend the optimal size.

What kind of warranty should I expect?

A robust warranty should cover both the product and installation. At M&M Gutters & Exteriors, we stand by our work with:

  • Workmanship Warranty: Covers the quality of the installation.
  • Material Warranty: Covers the gutter components against defects.
  • Lifetime Transferable Warranty: Our comprehensive warranty is transferable to new homeowners, adding value to your property.

Always clarify the specifics of any warranty before hiring a contractor.

Protect Your Investment with Expert Gutter Installation

Your home is one of your most valuable assets, and protecting it from the elements is a top priority. In Salt Lake City, with its unique blend of heavy snows, rapid thaws, and intense thunderstorms, a high-quality, professionally installed gutter system isn’t just a home improvement—it’s essential home protection.

We’ve seen the damage that inadequate or failing gutters can cause, from costly foundation repairs and flooded basements to deteriorating siding and eroded landscapes. By choosing M&M Gutters & Exteriors for your gutter installation Salt Lake City, you’re opting for proactive home maintenance that safeguards your property’s structural integrity, preserves its aesthetic appeal, and maintains its value for years to come.

Our decades of experience, commitment to quality materials, seamless installation techniques, and use of advanced tools like HOVER technology ensure that you receive a gutter system perfectly custom to your home and built to withstand Utah’s demanding weather. Don’t wait for the next storm to highlight a problem.

h1: Can Leaf Guards Be Installed on Existing Gutters?
author: Nathan Nuttall
content:
If you’ve spent hours of your spring on a ladder cleaning out your gutters, you might want to consider leaf guards. These simple guards can keep a significant amount of leaves and debris out of your gutters, so your job will be much easier next spring.
But if your gutters are still in good shape, you don’t want to deal with the hassle and cost of getting new ones. So let’s take a look at how these guards work to keep leaves out and whether or not they can be installed on existing gutters.

How Do Leaf Guards Work?

There are several different types of gutter guards, but they all do essentially the same thing: let water through and keep debris out. Most guards sit inside or on top of your gutters and act as a filter to anything that runs off your roof. While they won’t eliminate the need for cleaning your gutters or the risk of clogs, they certainly reduce the risk of damage to your home’s siding and foundation caused by gutter clogs and sitting water.

Types of Leaf Guards

Gutter guards are available in five primary types: screen, micro-mesh, reverse curve or surface tension, brush, and foam. Here’s a look at each type and how they work.

Screen

Screen guards are exactly what they sound like: a guard made of a wire or plastic grid that allows water through but blocks large debris and leaves. They are the easiest to install.
Simply lift the bottom row of shingles along the entire length of the gutter and slide the edge of the screen guard beneath the shingles. The weight of the shingles is what holds the guard in place. They are also one of the least expensive types of gutter guards.

They might be easy to install and inexpensive, but screen guards have some downsides. Since there are no screws or nails to secure them, they can be dislodged by high winds and heavy rainstorms. Some roof warranties may also be voided by installing the guards underneath the shingles, so be sure to check with the shingle manufacturer before you install a gutter guard using this installation method.

Micro-Mesh

Micro-mesh gutter guards are similar to screen guards but with a much smaller grid. They can be installed the same way as screen guards, but there are other options too. You can snap some micro-mesh guards directly onto the gutters. You can screw others into the fascia, the vertical strip of wood just above the gutter.

These kinds of gutter guards are ideal in locations that deal with high amounts of blowing sand and other fine particles that can clog gutters. They need to be cleaned more frequently than other gutters because the fine mesh can get clogged easily.

Reverse Curve

Reverse curve leaf guards are some of the most popular gutter guards and some of the more expensive options, too. They work by curving over and then dropping back into the gutter. So when water and debris are running off of your roof, the leaves, and debris fall right over the gutter onto the ground, while the water follows the reverse curve right into the gutter.

These guards are incredibly effective, but they aren’t as DIY friendly. They need to be attached correctly to the fascia at a certain angle. Reverse curve gutter guards installed incorrectly can cause water to run off with the debris and cause severe damage to your home’s siding and foundation. They are installed over the top of gutters, so they work very well with your existing gutters. Just make sure you pick a color that matches what you already have.

Brush

Brush guards are very popular for homeowners on a budget and those who like to do things themselves because they are inexpensive and ultra-easy to install. It’s almost like sticking a pipe cleaner inside of your gutters. They are made of a thick metal core surrounded by bristles.
All you have to do is cut the brush to the proper length and then fit it inside of your gutters. There’s no need to attach it to anything; once it slips in, it will stay in place until you take it out.

This style of gutter guard is tricky to clean and can get nasty after a few seasons, but they are highly effective at preventing clogs and keeping large debris out of your gutters.

Foam

Foam guards are similar to brush guards in price and ease of installation. They’re a popular choice for DIYers. They come in a triangle-shaped foam block that rests inside your gutters and acts like a sponge that lets the water flow through and keeps the leaves and branches out.

One major downside to foam gutters is that they don’t work well in extremely wet environments because they tend to overflow. The foam can also soak up a lot of water and get very heavy, causing damage to your gutters.

What To Look For

When choosing your gutter guards, opt for something high-quality, so you don’t have to replace them a few years down the road. Poor quality gutter guards can be worse than not having guards, so we highly recommend working with a professional gutter company for the best selection and professional installation.

M&M Gutters Offers Leaf Guards For Your Existing Gutters

Your home is one of the most significant purchases you will ever make, and it’s essential to protect it from rain and storm damage. That’s why M & M Gutters & Exteriors is here to help. We offer several different types of rain gutters and high-quality leaf guards that will work with your existing gutters.

We have installed thousands of gutter and leaf guard systems on homes across Northern Utah, including Lehi, Salt Lake City, Park City, Ogden, and more. We provide superior service to new construction, remodels, apartments, and even commercial buildings. We also offer siding installation and repair, leaf guards, and ice melt systems. Contact us today for an estimate!

title: Can You Grow Strawberries in Your Rain Gutters?
meta: The thought of strawberries in rain gutters may never have crossed your mind, but you can turn your gutters into a place to grow berries.
h1: Can You Grow Strawberries in Rain Gutters?
author: Nathan Nuttall
content:
Gardening in rain gutters is all the rage these days. However, quite a few plants thrive in a rain gutter environment. The thought of strawberries in rain gutters may never have crossed your mind, but you can turn your humdrum gutters into a place to grow rain gutter strawberries and much more.

Is It Possible to Grow Plants in Rain Gutters?

Yes. Rain gutters can be used as makeshift planters by filling them with soil and plants. They can be hung vertically or placed on a flat surface, making them a versatile option for small spaces or urban gardening. However, ensuring that the gutters are cleaned out properly and have adequate drainage to prevent water from building up and causing issues is important.

What Type of Plants Can You Grow in a Rain Gutter?

Many plants can be grown in a rain gutter, including herbs, succulents, small flowers, and vegetables.

Some examples of plants that may do well in a rain gutter include:

  • Herbs such as basil, thyme, and parsley
  • Succulents such as sedum, echeveria, and sempervivum
  • Small flowers such as pansies, petunias, and marigolds
  • Vegetables such as lettuce, radishes, and small varieties of tomatoes.

These are not the only plants that flourish in rain gutters.

Several fruits love making a rain gutter their home, including:

  • Strawberries – These fruits are an excellent option for rain gutters because they have shallow roots and are well-suited to container gardening.
  • Blueberries – Delicious pie-worthy blueberries can be grown in rain gutters. They prefer acidic soil and also need more watering than strawberries. However, they need more space than strawberries.
  • Raspberries – Raspberries are also a good option for rain gutters. They can be planted in the same way as strawberries and blueberries. In fact, you can plant all three side-by-side and have a berry bonanza growing in your rain gutters.
  • Blackberries – Blackberries, like raspberries and blueberries, can also be grown in rain gutters.
  • Currants – Currants are also well-suited to container gardening and can be grown in rain gutters.
  • Grapes – Grapes can be trained to grow on trellises or arbors — they generally thrive in these situations the most — but can also be grown in rain gutters.

Keep in mind that some of these fruits, like blueberries, currants, or grapes, require more space, more watering, and a specific soil that is different than what strawberries grow in, which means you’ll need to have enough space and the right environment to plant these particular fruits.

The Soil You Choose Is Vital to Successfully Growing Fruit in Your Rain Gutters

Let’s start with the type of soil you’ll need to grow your fruit:

Blueberries, raspberries, and blackberries prefer well-drained, acidic soil with a pH between 4.5 and 5.5. They also prefer soils high in organic matter and have good water-holding capacity. They also require high levels of organic matter and good drainage.

Currants and grapes prefer soil that is well-draining and slightly acidic. Currants like soil with a pH between 5.5 and 6.5, and grapes prefer soil with a pH between 6 and 7.

It’s important to note that these fruits may not grow well in soil with high alkaline levels. So, if your soil has a higher pH, you may need to amend it with sulfur or other acidic amendments to lower the pH.

Also, it’s important to pay attention to soil drainage. If the soil retains water, it’s necessary to improve drainage by adding coarse sand, rocks, or gravel.

It’s important to note that when growing plants in a rain gutter, you’ll want to select well-suited plants for the conditions. For example, the weather in your region will affect your plant’s ability to grow and thrive in your rain gutters.

It is also vital to ensure that the plants you choose to grow are manageable for the space available in your rain gutters. Also, the plants should be able to tolerate full sun and have similar watering needs.

As for Rain Gutter Strawberries:

Strawberries grow best in well-draining, loamy soil with a slightly acidic pH between 6.0 and 6.5. They prefer soil that is moist but not waterlogged, and they require ample access to sunlight. They also grow well in raised garden beds or containers with good drainage.

Ready To Start Planting?

Here are seven steps to follow to plant strawberries and other plants in a rain gutter successfully:

  1. First, purchase or gather rain gutters at least 2 feet in length. Clean them thoroughly to remove any debris or dirt.
  2. Next, drill holes in the bottom of the gutters for drainage. These holes should be spaced about 6 inches apart.
  3. Purchase strawberry plants or other fruit plants that are suitable for container gardening.
  4. Fill the gutters with a potting mix formulated for strawberries or other fruit plants. Make sure the soil is moist before planting.
  5. Plant the strawberry or fruit plants in the soil, leaving about 6 inches of space between each plant.
  6. Once the fruit starts to ripen, harvest them regularly to encourage continued production.
  7. Enjoy your delicious homegrown strawberries or other fruit!

Here are some tips for maintaining rain gutter strawberries:

  • Water regularly – Rain gutter strawberries require consistent moisture to grow, so make sure to water them regularly. It’s best to water them in the morning so the foliage can dry before evening.
  • Provide proper drainage – Rain gutters tend to hold water, so ensure your gutters have adequate drainage holes to prevent waterlogging.
  • Fertilize – Apply a balanced fertilizer every 4-6 weeks during the growing season to ensure that your strawberries have all the necessary nutrients to grow.
  • Prune – Prune off dead or diseased leaves and runners to encourage new growth.
  • Pest control – Keep an eye out for pests such as slugs, aphids, and spider mites, and take appropriate action to control them.
  • Provide support – As the strawberries grow, they may need support to keep them from falling out of the rain gutter.
  • Keep them in a sunny spot – Strawberries need full sun to grow, so make sure your rain gutter is in a sunny area.
  • Remove the old strawberries – Remove the old strawberries once they are done fruiting and replace them with new plants.

title: Can You Have a Metal Roof on a Home in Utah? - M&M Gutters & Exteriors
h1: Can You Have a Metal Roof on a Home in Utah?
author: M&M Gutters & Exteriors
content:
Are you thinking about adding a metal roof to your Utah home? You’ve come to the right place! Metal roofs are becoming more popular in our state because they are highly durable and well-suited to Utah’s weather conditions, from snowy winters in Logan to hot summers in Moab and St. George.

Read on to discover the pros and cons of metal roofing and find out if it’s a good fit for your house.

What Is Metal Roofing?

A metal roof is made of metal materials, like aluminum, copper, tin, or zinc, and functions like any other type of roof to provide protection. You can get a metal roof in several styles, colors, and finishes to create a unique look on your home.

Is a Metal Roof Cheaper Than Shingles?

Shingles are the most popular type of roofing because they are cost-effective and reliable. While metal roofing can be more expensive, it’s more durable and long-lasting and can withstand extreme weather better than other roofing materials.

How Long Does a Metal Roof Last in Utah?

If you’re wondering how long metal roofs last, we have good news! Proper maintenance means a metal roof can last between 40 and 70 years. So, while these roofs may have more upfront costs, they are still cost-effective since you won’t have to replace them often.

How Weather-Proof Are Metal Roofs?

Metal roofs are an excellent choice for Utah homes, as they can withstand our varied weather conditions. These roofs are sturdier, more water-resistant, and longer-lasting than other options, which helps ensure they’ll provide excellent protection for your Utah home, especially if you live in warmer climates like Moab or St. George.

What Is the Average Cost of a New Metal Roof?

The cost of metal home roofs will vary based on the size of your house, the material used, and the company you work with. An aluminum roof can cost between $11,000 and $35,000, while a copper roof ranges between $34,000 and $68,000.

What Are the Pros & Cons of a Metal Roof?

Like with any roofing material, there are always pros and cons to consider. Here are the pros and cons of a metal roof to understand when selecting a roof material for your home

Advantages of Metal Roofs

  • Durability: Metal roofs resist cracking, shrinking, and eroding, which means they can last longer.
  • Sustainability: Metal roofs are environmentally friendly and sustainable since metal is recyclable.
  • Life span: Metal roofs can last over 50 years, making them a more long-lasting solution.
  • Aesthetics: With multiple material options, metal roofs create a beautiful look that enhances curb appeal.
  • Energy efficiency: Metal roofs reflect heat instead of absorbing it, so they won’t make your home hotter hotter and are highly energy-efficient.
  • Fire- and storm-resistant: A metal roof is noncombustible and offers more protection from fire and severe weather.
  • Maintenance and care: Metal roofs need little maintenance, saving time, money, and effort.

Disadvantages of Metal Roofs

  • Noise: Many people are concerned that metal roofs are noisy during rain or hail storms, but insulation technology helps prevent this.
  • Upfront cost and affordability: Metal roofs offer long-term cost savings, though they can be more expensive upfront than other options.
  • Dents: Extreme weather events may cause dents on a metal roof. However, using high-quality materials can minimize this risk.
  • Limited by HOA: Some Homeowners’ Associations won’t allow metal roofs.
  • Installation: Metal roofs require more specialized installation skills than traditional roof options.
  • Contraction and expansion: Metal can expand or contract as temperatures fluctuate, but proper installation can reduce this problem.
  • Color fading: Metal roofs can fade over time, so they need to be sealed with a high-quality finish to prevent this.

What Are the Different Types of Metal Roofs?

When you’re considering adding a metal roof to your Utah home, you’ll have several beautiful options to choose from. Here are the different types of metal roofs we offer at M&M Gutters.

Aluminum

Copper

Steel

Tin

Zinc

What Makes M&M Gutters Roofs Different From Other Metal Roofing Brands?

At M&M Gutters, we have extensive experience installing and maintaining metal roofs in Utah. We’re committed to using top-quality materials and providing the best customer service to ensure you feel confident about switching to a metal roof.

Should I Get a Metal Roof?

Metal roofs are an excellent choice for Utah homes, but you should consider budget, aesthetic preferences, and home location before making your final decision. It’s a good idea to speak with roofing professionals, like those at M&M Gutters, to help you determine if a metal roof is right for you.

What Are the Environmental Benefits of Metal Roofs?

Metal roofs offer several environmental benefits to protect your home and reduce your carbon footprint. They are:

  • Recyclable: Metal roofs are primarily made from recycled materials and are 100% recyclable at the end of their lifespan.
  • Energy-efficient: Metal roofs reflect solar heat, resulting in lower cooling costs.
  • Long lifespan: Metal roofs can last up to 70 years with minimal maintenance.
  • Perfect for solar panels: If you plan to install solar panels, a metal roof is a great complement.

How Do I Maintain a Metal Roof?

Metal roofs are generally low-maintenance and require minimal upkeep to keep your roof in good condition. To maintain your metal roof, be sure to:

  • Check your roof after heavy winds, rain, and snowstorms.
  • Trim any overhanging tree branches.
  • Tighten loose screws from time to time.
  • Inspect your roof for signs of rust, scratches, and other damage to coatings.
  • Get a professional roof inspection every few years.

Reviewing this maintenance checklist can help keep your home protected.

Quote Your Next Project Today!

Discover the benefits of a metal roof by contacting M&M Gutters today. We’re ready to help you determine which type of metal roof is right for your Utah home. Get in touch with our team to discuss our work and get a quote on your next roof or home improvement project!

title: Can You Paint Vinyl Siding? - M&M Gutters & Exteriors
meta: Can you or should you paint your vinyl siding? Learn whether you can give your vinyl siding a fresh look with paint, from M&M Gutters experts.
h1: Can You Paint Vinyl Siding?
author: Nathan Nuttall
content:
Vinyl siding can be a great way to improve the look of your home. Not only will good looking siding boost curb appeal, but it also is versatile and doesn’t require a lot of maintenance. New siding, however, can be quite an investment depending on the size of the job and quality of siding you select. You may find yourself looking for less of a financial commitment.

If you’re in the market for a quick fix for old siding or just a new look, you may have asked, “Can vinyl siding be painted?” In short, the answer is yes. However, there are several things to take into consideration before painting. Before you pull the trigger on giving your home a facelift via paint, keep reading to learn more.

Your Vinyl Siding’s Warranty

The vinyl siding on your home likely came with a manufacturer’s warranty. It is also likely that a manufacturer (or home owner’s insurance) will not honor that warranty if the siding is painted. Prior to painting your siding, check the warranty information on your siding. It is possible that your warranty is already expired, invalid, or you may not be concerned about a void in warranty. If any of those are the case, painting the siding on your home might be right for you.

Surface Level Only

If you are looking to only make a cosmetic change on the exterior of your home, painting your vinyl siding may be the right choice (warranty aside). However, if you’ve noticed your old home is drafty or hot in the warmer months, you may need to go below the surface to fix the issue. Proper insulation may be missing from the exterior walls of your home. Painting your home will not allow you to resolve this issue.

Decide on an Investment

Painting your home can cost thousands of dollars. The exact cost varies based on the size of your home, but HomeGuide reports it ranges $1,800-$3,200. Many people choose to save a few dollars and make it a DIY project. If you do decide to do it yourself, don’t forget to take into account the additional tools you’ll need outside of paint (lots of paint!) and brushes (scaffolding, extenders, sprayers, window coverings, etc.).

New vinyl siding is definitely the more significant up-front investment. Higher in cost, but lower in maintenance as it doesn’t require touch-ups or much upkeep. It also comes with a warranty for many years and even lifetime guarantees; it also comes in many colors and finish options. You can expect to repaint your home every five or so years with minor touch-ups in between. Those paint jobs add up, making painting a costly investment over time. So it comes down to which investment you want to make: new siding or painting.

M&M Gutters & Exteriors

Painting vinyl siding is a definite option and one that many have chosen. It is important to look at the advantages and disadvantages of painting your vinyl siding because once it is done, it’s permanent!

If you are leaning towards or would like more information on vinyl siding, reach out to the professionals at M&M Gutters & Exteriors. Let us help you find a solution for the exterior of your home.

title: Catching Every Drop: How to Master Your Roof’s Rainwater Gutter System - M&M Gutters & Exteriors
meta: Master your rain water gutter roof system with expert sizing, slope, and material tips to prevent damage and protect your home.
h1: Catching Every Drop: How to Master Your Roof’s Rainwater Gutter System
author: M&M Gutters & Exteriors
content:
How to Optimize Your Rain Water Gutter Roof System

A well-designed rain water gutter roof system catches runoff at the roof edge, moves it through properly sized gutters and downspouts, and releases it safely away from your foundation. To get it right:

  1. Use at least 5-inch gutters for most homes, with 6-inch gutters for large or high-flow roof areas.
  2. Slope gutters about 1/16 inch per foot toward each downspout.
  3. Provide about 1 square inch of downspout area for every 100 square feet of roof drainage area.
  4. Extend discharged water away from the house so it cannot erode soil or soak the foundation.

Gutters are not just trim along the roofline. They protect siding, paint, landscaping, fascia, and the soil around your home. In Salt Lake City’s mix of spring runoff, summer storms, falling leaves, and winter snow, the details matter: gutter size, hanger spacing, drainage slope, guard selection, and where downspouts send water.

I’m Nathan Nuttall of M&M Gutters & Exteriors. For more than 30 years, our team has helped Utah homeowners plan and install rain water gutter roof systems alongside roofing, siding, and exterior improvements, making it easier to protect the whole home with one reliable team.

Key rain water gutter roof vocabulary:

  • PVC Rain Water Gutter
  • FRP Rainwater Gutter

Designing an Efficient Rain Water Gutter Roof System

Rainwater conveyance is an engineering challenge. When a storm rolls across the Wasatch Front, thousands of gallons of water cascade down your roof shingles in minutes. Without an engineered drainage strategy, that volume will overwhelm your eaves, saturate your siding, and pool around structural footings.

To prevent overflow, we calculate drainage capacity using the Rational Method formula:

$$Q = C times I times A times 0.0104$$

Where:

  • $Q$ is the peak runoff flow rate in gallons per minute (GPM).
  • $C$ is your roof catchment runoff coefficient (smooth metal roofs score around 0.90 to 0.95, while architectural asphalt shingles range from 0.80 to 0.90).
  • $I$ is the local rainfall intensity in inches per hour based on a design storm event.
  • $A$ is the roof footprint area in square feet.

Building codes commonly design residential conveyance for a 5-year or 10-year design storm, but a resilient roof gutter system should be at least 5 inches wide to handle a 100-year storm event without spilling over the front lip. For accurate calculations, calculating roof drainage capacity allows you to match your roof’s square footage against local precipitation data.

Sizing Principles for Your Rain Water Gutter Roof

A gutter is only as effective as the downspouts that drain it. If the downspouts are undersized, water backs up inside the trough, adding dead weight to the fascia board and spilling over the back edge.

As a standard rule of thumb, you must provide 1 square inch of downspout opening area for every 100 square feet of roof catchment area. For instance:

  • A standard 2-inch by 3-inch rectangular downspout yields 6 square inches of drainage area, accommodating up to 600 square feet of roof.
  • A 3-inch by 4-inch downspout offers 12 square inches of cross-sectional area, handling up to 1,200 square feet of roof area.

For massive residential roof planes or commercial buildings, an engineering study on optimal gutter dimensions demonstrates that matching high-capacity gutter widths with properly sized drop outlets minimizes hydraulic turbulence, letting water exit the roofline rapidly.

Critical Slope, Pitch, and Hanger Spacing Standards

Water cannot drain on a flat plane. Gutters must be sloped at a minimum fall of 1/16 inch per foot of run toward each downspout. On a 40-foot gutter run, this creates a total drop of 2.5 inches from the high end to the outlet drop. For standard residential eaves, a pitch ratio between 1 in 360 and 1 in 240 ensures that water moves quickly enough to carry light silt without splashing over the end caps. Flat roofs require a watertight membrane with a finished fall of 1 in 80 to avoid pooling before water reaches the scupper or external eave.

Hanger spacing provides the physical support needed to hold heavy water and ice:

  • Standard climate spacing: Mount heavy-duty hidden hangers every 3 feet (36 inches) on center, screwed directly through the sub-fascia into the structural rafter tails.
  • Heavy snow zones: Across high-elevation areas like Summit County, snow and ice loads can tear loose troughs right off the eaves. In these regions, shorten hanger spacing to 1 foot (12 inches) on center.

Choosing Gutter Profiles and Materials for Longevity

Gutter profile design directly governs water-carrying capacity and debris clearing. The two dominant profiles used across residential architecture are:

  • K-Style (Ogee Gutters): Featuring a flat back that mounts flush against the fascia board and an ornamental, crown molding-inspired outer face. The flat bottom and vertical walls allow K-style troughs to hold significantly more water than rounded profiles of equivalent width. A 6-inch K-style gutter remains the gold standard for handling high-volume roof runoff.
  • Half-Round Gutters: Shaped like a smooth, semi-circular trough. While half-round profiles carry less total volume than K-style profiles, their smooth curved bottom produces less hydraulic friction and reduces debris accumulation. They are mounted using external bracket hangers, making them popular for historic renovations and European-style architecture.

To eliminate leak points, seamless gutters are roll-formed on-site from single coils of .027-inch to .032-inch thick metal. Seamless runs can span up to 100 continuous feet without a joint, eliminating up to 90% of the leak risks found in sectional, box-store troughs.

Comparing Metal and Composite Gutter Options

Selecting the right material balances structural lifespan, corrosion resistance, and total investment:

  • Aluminum: The most popular residential choice. It is lightweight, completely rust-proof, and factory-finished in dozens of baked-on enamel colors. Seamless aluminum gutters formed from .027-inch or .032-inch stock routinely last 20 to 30+ years with minimal maintenance.
  • Copper: The pinnacle of architectural drainage. Copper never rusts and requires no paint. Over time, it develops a protective patina, transitioning from bright bronze to deep brown within several years, reaching a rich dark green patina by year twenty. Copper systems are joined with soldered seams and last 50 to 100 years.
  • Galvanized & Galvalume Steel: Zinc-coated steel provides extreme impact resistance against falling tree limbs and heavy snow slides. However, if the protective coating is scratched, moisture can eventually cause rust at standing water joints.
  • Fiberglass / FRP Composites: When evaluating the durability of FRP rainwater drainage, composite troughs offer total chemical and salt resistance, making them useful for specific industrial or architectural eaves.

When evaluating materials, review our guide on estimating your rain gutter installation cost to balance material lifespans with your overall project budget.

Thermal Expansion and Climate Considerations

All gutter materials expand and contract with seasonal temperature swings. For instance, rigid PVC has a thermal expansion coefficient of 0.06 mm/m°C. A 4-meter section of plastic gutter exposed to a temperature swing from −5°C in the winter to 25°C in the summer expands by up to 7.2 mm. Without specialized expansion slip joints, vinyl gutters can buckle or pull away from the fascia.

Understanding these dynamics is critical when protecting homes using PVC rainwater gutters, which require dedicated expansion gaps at every union. Metal gutters—especially seamless aluminum and steel—exhibit significantly lower thermal movement, keeping joints tight and fasteners secure through extreme seasonal shifts.

Integrating Gutter Guards, Debris Protection, and Rainwater Harvesting

A clogged gutter is no better than having no gutter at all. When deciduous leaves, pine needles, and roof shingle grit settle into the trough, they decompose into a dense, water-logged compost that blocks downspout openings.

  • Stainless Steel Micro-Mesh Guards: The most effective barrier available. Surgical-grade stainless steel mesh (openings under 50 microns) blocks fine sand, pine needles, and pollen while allowing high-velocity storm runoff to pull through via surface tension. Micro-mesh filters reduce gutter cleaning frequency by over 70%.
  • Reverse-Curve (Surface Tension) Hoods: Water flows over a curved nose into a narrow horizontal slot, while large leaves fall over the edge. These systems perform well with large broadleaf trees but can struggle to capture water during heavy downpours on steep roofs.
  • Perforated Drop-In Screens: Affordable perforated aluminum panels that keep out large oak and maple leaves, though small seeds, blossoms, and roof grit can still pass through the perforations.

Note on sizing: Fine screens and micro-mesh guards can derate water entry capacity by 10% to 20% during intense rainstorms. When installing gutter guards on high-pitch roofs, upsizing from a 5-inch to a 6-inch high-capacity gutter ensures no water overshoots the front edge.

How Rain Water Gutter Roof Conveyance Protects Your Home

Beyond protecting your foundation, your roof’s rainwater gutter system can serve as a primary catchment infrastructure for water conservation. Rainwater harvesting captures storm runoff and stores it for landscaping, urban gardens, and emergency supplies.

To maintain water quality in your storage cistern:

  1. Debris Filtration: Gutter micro-mesh guards act as a pre-filter, preventing large organic contaminants from entering downspout collection lines.
  2. First-Flush Diversion: The initial minutes of a rainstorm wash away airborne dust, bird droppings, and loose roof sediment. A first-flush diverter routes the first 10 to 50 gallons per 1,000 square feet of roof area away from the cistern into a drainage chamber before directing pure water into storage.
  3. Storage Integration: For detailed system design specifications, consult the Virginia Tech guide to rainwater harvesting systems.

Preventing Common Gutter Failures, Leaks, and Ice Dams

Winter weather presents severe challenges to roof drainage systems across Salt Lake, Davis, and Weber counties. When heat escapes through unconditioned attic spaces, it melts snow on the upper roof deck. As that meltwater runs down to the cold, uninsulated roof eaves and gutter troughs, it refreezes, creating thick ice dams.

Ice dams expand under shingles, rot structural wood fascia, and tear heavy gutter troughs straight off the eaves. Left unchecked, backed-up water leaks into exterior wall cavities.

To protect your eaves from winter damage:

  • Improve Attic Insulation & Ventilation: Keep the roof deck uniformly cold by sealing ceiling air leaks and maintaining clear soffit-to-ridge airflow.
  • Install Self-Regulating Heat Cables: Read our guide on proven methods for gutter ice prevention to protect vulnerable eave sections.
  • Targeted Cable Routing: When integrating rain gutter heating systems, lay cables in a zig-zag pattern along the roof edge and run them directly inside the gutter trough and downspouts to maintain a continuous, open melt path.

Frequently Asked Questions about Rain Water Gutter Roof Systems

What size gutters are best for high-rainfall storm events?

For high-volume storm events or roofs with long rafters and steep slopes, 6-inch K-style seamless gutters paired with 3-inch by 4-inch downspouts provide the best protection. A 6-inch K-style trough holds nearly 40% more water volume than a standard 5-inch gutter, preventing overflow during sudden, intense downpours.

How does roof pitch impact gutter positioning and water capture?

Steeper roofs (such as 8:12 to 12:12 pitches) cause runoff to accelerate rapidly down the roof plane. If a gutter is mounted too high or positioned incorrectly, this high-velocity sheet flow will shoot straight over the front lip. For steep-pitch roofs, position the gutter drop roughly 20 mm (3/4 inch) below the extended roof line slope to intercept the water trajectory cleanly without overshooting.

How often should gutters and downspouts be inspected and cleaned?

Inspect and clean your gutters at least twice per year: once in late autumn after all leaves have dropped, and once in early spring to clear winter silt, grit, and inspect for freeze-thaw damage. If your roofline is surrounded by heavy pine or mature oak trees, schedule quarterly checkups or install micro-mesh gutter guards to maintain open drainage paths year-round.

Conclusion

Your roof and gutter system work together as your home’s first line of defense against water intrusion. When properly engineered—with accurate sizing calculations, correct slope pitch, heavy-duty hanger spacing, and integrated debris protection—your gutters protect your home’s foundation, siding, and roof structure for decades.

At M&M Gutters & Exteriors, we bring over 30 years of hands-on expertise to every home improvement project across Salt Lake County, Utah County, Summit County, and Northern Utah. Using our 3D visualization technology via HOVER, we map your home’s exact exterior dimensions to install custom, on-site roll-formed seamless gutter systems tailored to your specific roof pitch and snow load conditions.

Ready to upgrade your home’s rainwater management? You can easily schedule a professional rain gutters installation with M&M Gutters & Exteriors today for a comprehensive on-site assessment and estimate.

title: Choosing Your Felt A Deep Dive into ASTM D226 Type 1 and Type 2 - M&M Gutters & Exteriors
meta: Choose the right roofing felt. Explore 30 astm d226's benefits, specs, and compare underlayments for ultimate roof protection.
h1: Choosing Your Felt A Deep Dive into ASTM D226 Type 1 and Type 2
author: M&M Gutters & Exteriors
content:
Why Understanding 30 ASTM D226 Matters for Your Roofing Project

30 ASTM D226 refers to Type II asphalt-saturated organic felt underlayment, a heavier roofing underlayment that serves as a critical secondary water barrier beneath your primary roofing materials.

Quick Answer: What You Need to Know About 30 ASTM D226

  • Type: ASTM D226 Type II asphalt-saturated organic felt
  • Weight: 52-56 lbs per roll
  • Coverage: 216 square feet per roll (36″ x 72′)
  • Primary Use: Underlayment beneath asphalt shingles, metal, and tile roofs
  • Key Benefit: Heavier and more durable than Type I (#15 felt)
  • Certifications: Florida Building Code approved, Miami-Dade approved, UL specifications met
  • Composition: Organic felt saturated with asphalt, often made from 100% post-consumer recycled material
  • Exposure Limits: 60 days (single-ply), 6 months (two-ply)

When planning a roofing project, the underlayment choice is critical. It directly impacts your roof’s longevity and protection against Utah’s harsh weather.

The difference between Type I and Type II felt matters. Type I (#15 felt) is lighter for standard jobs, while Type II (#30 felt) is heavier and more durable, ideal for steep-slope roofs and all-climate performance. Industry standards recognize 30 ASTM D226 Type II for its superior tear resistance and water protection in demanding applications.

This heavier felt is a breathable secondary barrier applied over the roof deck. It protects against moisture, prevents dry rot and mold, and validates most roofing warranties.

I’m Nathan Nuttall at M&M Gutters & Exteriors. With over 30 years of experience serving Utah homeowners, I’ve seen quality underlayment like 30 ASTM D226 Type II prevent premature roof failure. Understanding these felt types helps you make an informed decision to protect your home investment.

Understanding the Role of Roofing Felt

Think of your roof in layers. While shingles are the visible first defense against weather, roofing felt is the crucial backup layer beneath them.

At M&M Gutters & Exteriors, we explain to our Salt Lake City clients that roofing felt, or underlayment, is a secondary water barrier. It protects your roof deck from moisture that gets past shingles, which is critical in Utah’s climate of heavy snow and intense storms. This layer prevents water from reaching the wooden deck and your home’s interior. Learn more in our guide on What is Roofing Felt.

Asphalt-saturated felt is a traditional, effective underlayment. It’s an organic felt material infused with asphalt to make it water-resistant and durable.

The quality of these materials is ensured by organizations like ASTM International. ASTM, formerly the American Society for Testing and Materials, sets technical standards for a wide range of products. For roofing felt, their standards provide a benchmark for manufacturers and a performance guarantee for consumers.

What is the ASTM D226 Standard?

When we talk about 30 ASTM D226, we’re referring to a specific standard from ASTM International, a global organization that sets benchmarks for product quality, safety, and performance. For roofing, these standards are vital for ensuring reliability and consistency.

The ASTM D226 standard, titled “Standard Specification for Asphalt-Saturated Organic Felt Used in Roofing and Waterproofing,” defines the requirements for this type of underlayment. You can find the full details in the Standard Specification for Asphalt-Saturated Organic Felt.

This underlayment is made from organic felt, often using 100% post-consumer recycled material. This makes 30 ASTM D226 an eco-friendly choice for Utah homeowners seeking sustainable options.

The organic felt is then saturated with asphalt, changing it into a flexible, water-resistant barrier. This process is crucial for creating the secondary weather protection needed in Utah’s climate, from Salt Lake County to Summit County.

Type I vs. Type II Felt

The ASTM D226 standard has two main classifications, often known by their traditional “pound” weights:

  • Type I Felt (often called #15 felt): The lighter option, traditionally weighing about 15 pounds per square (100 sq ft). It’s flexible and suitable for standard roofing applications needing a basic secondary barrier.
  • Type II Felt (often called #30 felt): This is 30 ASTM D226. It’s significantly heavier (about 30 pounds per square), offering increased durability and tear resistance. We recommend it for demanding applications like steep-slope roofs and in harsh weather areas across Northern Utah. Its robust composition provides a superior barrier against moisture and wear.

A Closer Look at 30 ASTM D226 Type II Felt

30 ASTM D226 Type II felt is a robust barrier built for serious, long-term protection. Its substantial nature hints at the durability it provides.

It’s a versatile underlayment for asphalt shingles, metal, and tile roofs, making it a professional go-to. Manufactured for all-climate performance, it reliably handles everything from Salt Lake City’s summer sun to Summit County’s heavy snow. Its core function is to act as a secondary weather-resistant barrier, catching any moisture that gets past the primary roofing and protecting the roof deck.

Key Specifications of 30 ASTM D226 Felt

Understanding the specifications of 30 ASTM D226 felt highlights its robust design. These numbers directly relate to its performance and your roof’s integrity.

  • Weight per Roll: Typically 52 to 56 pounds, indicating its density and durability. This heft is what gives it the “30 lb” designation per square (100 sq ft).
  • Roll Dimensions: A standard roll is 36 inches wide and about 72 feet long, designed for efficient installation and proper overlap.
  • Coverage Area: One roll covers approximately 216 square feet. Professionals factor in overlap when calculating the total material needed.
  • Material Composition: Manufactured from superior quality organic felt, often made from 100% post-consumer recycled material, making it a sustainable choice.
  • Asphalt Saturation Level: The felt is thoroughly saturated with asphalt, creating a dense, water-resistant barrier.
  • Walkable Non-Skid Surface: The felt’s natural non-skid surface improves safety for roofing crews during installation, especially on the steep-slope roofs common in Utah.

Benefits of Using 30 ASTM D226 Underlayment

Choosing 30 ASTM D226 Type II felt for your Utah roofing project offers significant advantages for your roof’s longevity and performance.

  • Improved Durability: Its heavier construction withstands the stress of installation and exposure, leading to a more resilient roof.
  • Superior Water Resistance: The asphalt saturation creates a critical secondary barrier against water from wind-driven rain or ice dams.
  • Improved Tear Resistance: It’s less likely to rip or puncture during installation, ensuring a continuous, effective barrier.
  • Validates Roofing System Warranties: Using a compliant underlayment like 30 ASTM D226 is often required by manufacturers to keep your shingle or metal roof warranty valid.
  • Breathability (Permeability): Organic felt is breathable, allowing moisture vapor from the attic to escape. This prevents condensation, mold, and rot within the roof structure.
  • Prevents Dry Rot and Mold: By managing moisture from both outside and inside, it helps keep the roof deck dry and structurally sound.
  • Cost-Effectiveness: While the upfront cost is slightly higher than Type I, its superior durability and protection make it a smarter long-term investment, reducing the risk of future repairs.

How ASTM D226 Felt Compares to Other Underlayments

Roofing underlayment comes in several types. Understanding how 30 ASTM D226 Type II felt compares to Type I felt and modern synthetics is key to choosing the right option for your Salt Lake City home. Our guide to Roofing Materials and Types offers more detail.

Let’s look at a quick comparison:

FeatureASTM D226 Type I (#15 Felt)ASTM D226 Type II (#30 Felt)Synthetic Underlayment
WeightLighter (approx. 15 lbs/sq)Heavier (approx. 30 lbs/sq)Very Lightweight
DurabilityGoodExcellentSuperior
Water ResistanceGoodVery GoodExcellent
Tear ResistanceModerateHighVery High
PermeabilityBreathableBreathableOften breathable (varies)
WalkabilityModerateGood (natural non-skid)Excellent (non-skid coatings)
Exposure LimitShorter (days)Longer (60 days/6 months)Very Long (up to 6-12 months)
CostLowerModerateHigher

Traditional vs. Modern Materials:
Asphalt-saturated felts (Type I and II) are the traditional, proven choice. Type I is economical for standard jobs, while 30 ASTM D226 Type II offers better durability for severe weather or steep pitches.

Synthetic underlayments are a modern alternative. They are lightweight, extremely tear-resistant, and can be exposed to weather longer. While they offer superior water resistance and safety features, they typically come at a higher cost.

Choosing the Right Underlayment for Your Project:
The best choice depends on your project, budget, and primary roofing material.

  • Type I Felt: A good, low-cost option for standard shingle roofs on moderate slopes.
  • 30 ASTM D226 Type II Felt: An excellent balance of performance and value for steep-slope roofs, metal or tile roofs, and homes in the varied climates across Salt Lake, Utah, Davis, and Weber Counties.
  • Synthetic Underlayment: The preferred choice for premium systems needing maximum tear resistance or long-term exposure before the final roof is installed.

When considering options like a Metal Roof vs Shingles, the underlayment choice is also a key factor. Our team at M&M Gutters & Exteriors can help you select the optimal underlayment for Utah’s unique environment.

Installation Best Practices and Code Compliance

Proper installation is essential for 30 ASTM D226 Type II felt to perform correctly. At M&M Gutters & Exteriors, we follow strict guidelines for every Salt Lake City home. Roof deck preparation is the first step: the deck must be clean, dry, and smooth, with any damage repaired.

Proper lapping is key to creating a water-shedding barrier. This involves overlapping the felt rolls correctly:

  • Headlap (vertical overlap): At least 2 inches for slopes 4:12 or greater; 4 inches for lower slopes.
  • Sidelap (horizontal overlap): At least 2 inches.

Fastening is critical to prevent blow-offs in Northern Utah’s winds. We use plastic cap nails, which have a wide cap that seals the nail hole and improves the system’s water resistance.

Sealing around penetrations like vents and chimneys is paramount. The underlayment must be carefully cut and sealed with flashing to maintain the moisture barrier. This diligence helps Prevent Roof Damage During Utah Winters.

Certifications and Building Codes

Adhering to building codes is non-negotiable for a safe, compliant roof.

  • Code Approvals: Many 30 ASTM D226 products meet stringent standards like the Florida Building Code, Miami-Dade County approval, and UL specifications. This demonstrates high quality and resilience, reassuring for Utah’s challenging climate.
  • Local Code Verification: For homeowners in Salt Lake, Utah, Summit, Tooele, Davis, and Weber counties, verifying local code is essential. M&M Gutters & Exteriors is well-versed in Utah’s local codes and ensures every project is compliant.
  • Warranty Compliance: Manufacturers require proper, code-compliant installation of an approved underlayment to validate the primary roofing warranty. Using 30 ASTM D226 Type II felt correctly protects your long-term investment.

Frequently Asked Questions about ASTM D226 Felt

We often get excellent questions from homeowners in Utah about various roofing materials. Here are some of the most common inquiries regarding 30 ASTM D226 Type II felt:

Is #30 felt environmentally friendly?

Yes, 30 ASTM D226 felt can be an environmentally conscious choice. Many manufacturers produce the organic felt from 100% post-consumer recycled material, reducing landfill waste. Some also use domestic asphalt from local sources, which lowers transportation emissions. Using these materials can even contribute to LEED points for green building certification, making it a sustainable option for your Utah home.

Where can I buy #30 felt and what does it cost?

30 ASTM D226 Type II felt is widely available at building suppliers, lumberyards, and retailers like True Value. You might find brands like Tarco’s Asphalt Roofing Felt Type II, ASTM D-226 Gold Lined, 30 Lb., readily available.

Pricing varies based on brand, quantity, supplier, and market conditions. Buying in bulk typically lowers the per-roll cost. For homeowners in the Salt Lake City area, M&M Gutters & Exteriors sources materials directly from suppliers, often at better rates. We include the cost of high-quality underlayment in our project quotes. Understanding The Cost of a Roof Replacement Roof Care in Utah can provide a helpful overview. While DIY purchase is possible, professional installation is paramount for performance.

How long can #30 felt be exposed to weather?

While durable, 30 ASTM D226 felt is not a permanent roof surface and has exposure limits:

  • Single-ply applications: Approximately 60 days.
  • Two-ply applications: Up to 6 months.

It is critical to cover the underlayment with the primary roofing material within these timeframes. Prolonged exposure can lead to UV degradation, water absorption, and physical damage from wind or foot traffic. At M&M Gutters & Exteriors, we prioritize timely installation to ensure the underlayment performs as a robust secondary barrier for the life of your roof.

Making the Right Choice for Your Utah Roof

Understanding underlayment like 30 ASTM D226 is key to making an informed roofing decision. We’ve seen how Type I felt offers a standard solution, while 30 ASTM D226 Type II steps up with improved durability, tear resistance, and overall protection, making it a stellar choice for Utah’s diverse climate.

Quality underlayment is a critical secondary defense against moisture and is vital for validating your roof’s warranty. Skimping on this foundational layer risks the longevity of your entire roof.

Choosing the right underlayment is about protecting your investment. Your roof is one of the most crucial components of your home. By selecting a high-quality product like 30 ASTM D226 Type II felt and ensuring professional installation, you are investing in peace of mind and the long-term health of your home.

For expert advice on materials for your Salt Lake City home’s exterior, trusted installation, and a partner who understands Utah’s unique climate challenges, turn to the experienced team at M&M Gutters & Exteriors. We’re here to help you make choices that ensure your roof performs flawlessly for decades. Explore our professional roofing services today and let us help you build a resilient, beautiful roof that lasts.

h1: Cleaning Your Rain Gutters is Absolutely Necessary
author: Nathan Nuttall
content:
Rain gutters are an important part of the exterior of your home. They prevent large icicles from forming and prevent any damage to your foundation. They protect the walls of your home and capture and divert water away from your home or landscaping. They reduce the number of puddles or icy areas on walkways.

Over time, clogged gutters can cause fascia boards and soffit to deteriorate and eventually rot. Keeping your rain gutters clean and clear of leaves and debris is absolutely necessary.

Here are some tips and tricks on how to clean your rain gutters.

Frequency

Your gutters should be clean out at least once a year. If you have large overhanging trees nearby, they should be cleaned twice yearly. If at any point your gutters become clogged, clean them right away or as soon as possible. Big storms and strong winds tend to fill up gutters quickly, so be sure to check them any time those occur.

How to Clean Your Gutters

Step 1: Get your gear on and ready. You’ll need a pair of gloves, some safety glasses, a ladder, a trowel or your favorite gutter cleaning tool, a couple of buckets (one for debris, the other for tools), a long garden hose and nozzle, and a long-sleeved shirt to protect your arms.

Step 2: Remove any and all gutter covers/guards.

Step 3: Starting near a downspout, remove the larger leaves and other debris with your hands, a trowel, or other tool and discard them. Keeping a bucket hooked to your ladder helps save you from treks up and down your ladder.

Step 4: Use your hose and nozzle or a gutter-cleaning attachment to clear out the finer material in your gutter.

Step 5: If your gutter is not draining, check for clogs in your downspout strainer or downspout.

Step 6: Verify your gutter is securely fastened and does not appear to be loose.

Step 7: Once your gutters are draining properly, be sure to replace the strainer and any guards removed.

Helpful Pro Tips

  • Be sure to check the weather forecast prior to cleaning your gutters. Leaves and debris that have had time to dry out are much easier to clean.
  • If you know there’s a leak but are unsure where it is, use a bucket to fill the gutter with water and watch for the leak. Just make sure you give the gutter time to dry before repairs take place.
  • Add the leaves and other debris found in your gutters to your compost piles.
  • Consider having leaf guards installed on your gutters. Leaf guards help keep leaves, pine needles, and other debris out of your gutters. There are several options to choose from and many solutions to accommodate your specific needs. Call M&M Gutters today for more information about leaf guards and available options.

Safety

It is not recommended that you clean, maintain, or repair your gutters from your roof. You should always use a firmly planted ladder and closely follow ladder safety instructions and recommendations. Make sure the ground below the ladder is clear. Firmly attach your buckets to your ladder with hooks.
