h1: Why You Shouldn’t Install Your Rain Gutters Yourself
author: Nathan Nuttall
content:
The internet is a resourceful place to start DIY projects, and you might feel tempted to install your own rain gutters. However, rain gutter installation is a lot more serious and involved than crafts. Rain gutters force water to slide off your roof. Your home needs rain gutters, as gutters protect your roof, driveway, sidewalks, and the structure of your home. Rain gutters prevent soil erosion, so your flower beds will always be protected.

Every year, over 500,000 people suffer from ladder-related injuries according to the American Academy of Orthopedic Surgeons. You might think you can take on rain gutter installation, but then you reach the top of your ladder and realize this job is not for you. To avoid becoming part of the scary statistic mentioned above, it’s best that you leave rain gutter installation to the experts. Here’s what can go wrong if you try installing rain gutters at home.

You might injure yourself

If you fall off your ladder while installing a gutter, it isn’t a question of if you’ll fracture a bone, it’s a question of how many bones you’ll fracture. Ladder falls result in bone fractures, and that’s the best-case scenario. Concussions are also a common possibility. You might end up paralyzed. As frightening as this sounds, ladder falls also result in death. If you end up injured as a result of installing your own gutters, the price of your medical bills will be exponentially higher than the cost of contracting an expert to install your gutters. This defeats the purpose of installing gutters on your own.

It’s not as easy as it looks

Gutter installation isn’t as accessible as you think. There’s a reason why the gutter installation is a profession of its own. You need adequate training and materials to successfully install gutters at home. Moreover, you’ll need to know how to detect problems with your gutters such as rotting fascia boards, water damage, or even roof shingle repair. Experts who install gutters on a day-to-day basis have an eye for these common gutter problems, whereas you might not. Not only is gutter installation difficult, but it’s also expensive. In between the costs of buying the gutters, hangers, a tall enough ladder, clips, downspouts, and adhesive, you’ll be spending more money. Professionals already own all these materials, and they purchase them wholesale. You’d have to buy each part individually, and the costs rack up fast. Realistically, you probably won’t even have space in your car to transport these goods back to your house because gutters usually come in ten-foot sections.

You’ll get what you paid for

The gutters that you find at your home improvement store will not be of the highest quality. These gutters are pliable, and they will easily be distorted. If your ladder rests on your gutter, the ladder will dent the gutter. A hard bump on your roofline will also harm your gutters. These difficulties will cause you to restart your gutter installation process over and over again. Many professional companies now offer the option of seamless gutters, which are modern and aesthetically pleasing. Gone are the days of fastening multiple gutter sections together.

You’ll hardly see anyone in your neighborhood install their own gutters, and for good reason. Save yourself the potential injuries and money by contacting M&M Gutters today. From Weber County to Utah County, our experts will work around your busy schedule.

title: Wood Siding Maintenance Tips - M&M Gutters & Exteriors
meta: Wood is a popular choice for home siding. Keep your wood siding in top condition with these essential maintenance tips from the experts at M&M Gutters
h1: Wood Siding Maintenance Tips
author: Nathan Nuttall
content:
When choosing a siding for your house, you can’t go wrong with wood. The beautiful and natural look of wood is classic. Whether you go with shingles, panels, and another style, wood is always a winner. There are not only a wide variety of styles but also a variety of kinds. You can go with pine, cedar, fir, redwood, etc. Each of these will add their own look to your property.

Properly caring for wood siding helps it last much longer. Because the side of your house is vulnerable to the elements, wood side can rot with exposure to excessive moisture. But this is not always the case—sealing your siding and cleaning it regularly will help you maintain it longer.

1. Choosing a Sealant

Wood siding will natural expand and contract as temperature and humidity levels change. When left unprotected, paint will chip, caulk will separate, and water can potentially seep into the siding, leaving it vulnerable to mold, mildew, and rotting.

To protect your wood siding and make it last longer—you need to seal it. You can do this with paint, stain, or sealant. Paint will need to be replaced about every five years—possibly less if you live in a humid climate. Staining will penetrate wood fibers and seal out moisture. Sealants will help to prevent moisture damage and all the wood siding to retain its natural coloring. If you go with sealant, you’ll need to reapply it about every two years.

2. Cleaning Your Siding

About once a year, clean your wood siding. This can be done with warm water, soap, and a soft bristled brush. If you have any sections that are prone to mold growth, use a fungus-killing cleanser to clear away any potential growth. Be sure to thoroughly rinse with clean water.

3. Getting Rid of Rust Stains

Rust stains are common in wood siding—usually from nails or screws coming in contact with moisture. To remove these stains, combine warm water with oxalic acid. Wear protective eye gear when working with this solution. Apply the solution to the stain and scrub the stain away with a soft bristle brush. Rinse the area thoroughly with water.

4. Replacing Damaged Siding

If you have siding coming that needs to be replaced, you’ll likely want to contact a professional. Siding can be damaged over time, from an accident, or some exposure to the elements. Whether it’s a small fix like a panel or two, or an entire house that needs replacing, call in the pros. M&M Gutters will have your house looking new in no time.

5. Preventing Damage

Wooden siding is vulnerable to water infiltration. Because of this, you should check your caulk regularly and reapply as needed. This could save you from needing to replace wood panels. You can also prevent some damage by ensuring that no bushes, trees, or other shrubbery touches the wood siding. All foliage conducts moisture and that moisture will find its way into your siding, leading to rotting.

title: Year-Round House Maintenance Checklist for Utah Residents
meta: Learn all that you need to maintain your homes interior and exterior all year around for Utah resident to combat the hot summers and cold winters.
h1: Year-Round House Maintenance Checklist: Gutters and Roofs in Utah
author: M&M Gutters & Exteriors
content:
As a homeowner, it’s essential to maintain your property year-round. Proactive maintenance prevents you from having to make sudden, expensive repairs and keep your home a safe place to live, but it also preserves the value of what is probably one of your biggest investments.

For long-time and first-time homeowners alike, we’ve put together this house maintenance checklist to walk you through the most important maintenance tasks you’ll want to carry out for each season of the year, taking a special focus on gutter and roof maintenance.

The Importance of Year-Round Maintenance

Here are just a few good reasons to prioritize year-round home maintenance:

Save Money in the Short-Term & Long-Term

Regular maintenance on your home is a great way to save money. For one, when you follow an annual home maintenance checklist, you’ll be more likely to catch minor damage before it becomes a larger issue that is much more expensive to fix. Additionally, a regular house maintenance schedule will also maintain or even increase your home’s monetary value, ensuring that your investment stays a smart one.

Enhance Energy Efficiency

By paying attention to signs of wear and tear, you can prevent the outside elements from affecting the climate-controlled environment of your home’s interior, wasting the energy and money you spend on heating and cooling. Tasks like sealing gaps and cracks, insulating, and servicing your HVAC system can greatly improve your home’s energy efficiency, saving you money on utilities and helping the environment.

Maintain Comfort, Safety, & Livability

A home that receives regular maintenance isn’t just safer to live in. It’s also more comfortable. When you follow a regular house maintenance schedule, It ensures that your heating, cooling, and plumbing systems work correctly and keep the home livable. It also allows you to scrutinize your home and recognize hazards to your health and safety, like roof leaks, faulty wiring, loose handrails, and more.

Compliance With Warranty Requirements

Many of the warranties that homeowners receive for the systems in their homes will require maintenance as an important condition of coverage. By keeping up with the maintenance requirements of your home’s warranties, you remain eligible for warranty payouts should anything malfunction, saving money on possibly expensive repairs.

Seasonal Maintenance Tasks

Following a structured maintenance schedule is vital to keeping your home in its best condition. By carrying out a customized home maintenance regimen, your house can be ready to face the unique challenges that each season brings.

Spring Maintenance Tips

Spring is the season of renewal, making it a great time to freshen up your home after a potentially harsh winter. Here are a few home maintenance tasks to tackle in the spring.

  • Inspect and clean gutters: After fall and winter, you’ll likely have leaves, ice, and other debris in your gutters, which can clog them if left unchecked. Clean out your gutters thoroughly to allow them to drain properly and prevent your roof and foundation from getting water damaged.
  • Check for roof damage: Take a moment in the spring to examine your roof for any signs of damage. This might show up as loose or missing shingles or cracks. If you repair these issues early before they grow in severity, you can potentially save a lot of money on more costly repairs, like leaks and water damage in the rainy season. Schedule an annual roof inspection by a professional to ensure your roof stays intact.
  • Inspect siding and paint: Inspect your siding and exterior paint to determine if there is any new wear or damage. If necessary, repaint or repair your home’s exterior, both for cosmetic issues and to ensure that you’re adequately insulated and protected from the elements when you’re inside.
  • Service your HVAC system: After a busy winter of heating your home, but before a scorching summer full of cooling, spring makes for an ideal time to service your HVAC system. Each spring, clean or replace filters, inspect the system for leaks and ensure everything is running efficiently.
  • Inspect windows and doors: Improve your home’s energy efficiency by checking for drafts in all your windows and doors. If you can feel airflow in these areas when closed, seal whatever gaps or cracks are causing them.

Summer Home Care

Spring is the season of renewal, making it a great time to freshen up your home after a potentially harsh winter. Here are a few home maintenance tasks to tackle in the spring.

  • Inspect and clean gutters: Summer can bring some heavy rainstorms, so it’s another good opportunity to inspect and clean the gutters to prevent water damage.
  • Trim trees and shrubs: If the vegetation around your house has overgrown, it can not only damage the plants themselves in a bad windstorm but there’s also a potential for your trees and shrubs to damage the roof and siding. Keep your larger plants trimmed back to prevent their limbs from coming into contact with your home.
  • Check and seal exterior cracks: Inspect the exterior of your home to address any cracks or gaps. Seal up any of these breaks to keep the house insulated.
  • Test smoke and carbon monoxide detectors: Open windows and running fans can change up the airflow in your home, so summer is an excellent time to ensure that all of your alarms and detectors are working correctly.

Fall House Maintenance

As the weather starts to cool off in the fall, you’ll want to prepare your home for the season ahead. Here are some home maintenance tasks to carry out each autumn.

  • Clean gutters: With falling leaves clogging your gutters, fall is another opportunity to clean them out. This will help you avoid ice dams and possible water damage come wintertime.
  • Inspect and clean chimneys and fireplaces: When improperly maintained, Fireplaces and wood-burning stoves can create a buildup of creosote in your chimney, which can lead to house fires. Before you get into peak fireplace season each year, have a professional clean and inspect your fireplace and chimney to keep your home safe.
  • Seal gaps and cracks: As the temperatures drop, you’ll want to ensure that your home is well-insulated and your heating system is energy-efficient. Seal any gaps or cracks you find around windows or doors at this time.
  • Service your heating system: Service your heating system to ensure that it’s up to the task of warming your home before the colder months officially set in.
  • Prepare for snow removal: If your neighborhood gets a lot of snow in the winter, take this opportunity to prepare by getting the necessary tools and equipment ready for snow removal, from shovels, salt, and blowers to four-wheelers and plow blades, depending on your needs.

Winter Homeowner’s Maintenance Checklist

As winter sets in, you’ll need to give your home a little extra attention to ensure that your home can hold up against the snow, ice, and cold, keeping you safe and comfortable.

    • Clear snow and ice: By regularly removing snow and ice from your walkways, driveways, and roof, you’ll not only be able to get full use of your home’s exterior, but you’ll also be able to prevent accidents and injuries and also prevent unnecessary structural damage to your concrete and home.
    • Monitor for ice dams: Stay on the lookout for ice dams on your home’s roof. Ice dams can add excess weight to your roof and lead to leaks and water damage. Safely remove these whenever you see them form. If you experience frequent ice dams, consider installing heat cables on your roof to prevent ice buildup.
    • Check insulation: Insulation is essential to prevent the heat you’ve generated from escaping. Stay warm and lower your energy bills by inspecting and servicing your home’s insulation.
    • Inspect and clean furnace filters: Furnace filters need to be regularly replaced or cleaned to keep both the air quality of your home and the energy efficiency of your heating system high.
    • Prevent frozen pipes: Any exposed pipes should be adequately insulated to prevent freezing. If you need to travel for an extended period during the winter, it’s a good idea to leave your faucets dripping slightly, as this keeps the water moving through the pipes so it doesn’t freeze.

    Make M&M Gutters & Exteriors Part of Your House Maintenance Schedule

    Year-round maintenance is essential to keeping your home comfortable, livable, and safe, all while saving money and energy. By following a well-planned house maintenance checklist and getting professional assistance with your gutter and roofing needs from M&M Gutters & Exteriors, you can make your homeownership experience worry-free.

Why Finding the Right Rain Gutter Parts Matters for Your Home

Rain gutter parts near me are essential for protecting your home from water damage, foundation issues, and costly repairs. Finding quality parts locally, whether for a single downspout elbow or a full system overhaul, saves time and keeps your home safe.

Quick Answer: Where to Find Rain Gutter Parts Near You:

  • M&M Gutters & Exteriors – Your Salt Lake City expert for professional-grade parts, seamless gutters, and installation.
  • Online Ordering – Many suppliers offer local pickup or delivery.
  • Professional Suppliers – Access premium materials like copper and custom lengths through experienced contractors.

Understanding your gutter system is the first step. Clogged gutters can lead to foundation damage averaging $5,000 in repairs, making the right parts crucial. Your system includes gutters (troughs), downspouts, elbows, hangers, miters (corners), end caps, and splash blocks. A failure in one part can compromise the entire system.

The main challenge is finding quality replacements locally. While hardware stores stock basic components, specialized parts and seamless gutters often require a professional supplier who understands Utah’s climate.

If you want a broader background on how gutters fit into home drainage systems, the general overview at Rain gutter is a helpful external reference.

I’m Nathan Nuttall, and for over 30 years at M&M Gutters & Exteriors, I’ve helped Utah homeowners find the right rain gutter parts near me. This guide will cover what you need, where to find it, and when to call the pros.

Anatomy of a Gutter System: Understanding the Key Components

Think of your home’s gutter system as its circulatory system for water. Each component must work in harmony to move water safely away from your home. At M&M Gutters & Exteriors, we ensure every part of your system in Salt Lake City and surrounding counties functions perfectly.

Here are the essential players in this water-management team:

  • Gutters (Troughs): These horizontal channels along your roof’s edge are the first line of defense, catching rainwater and snowmelt. They channel water toward the downspouts, preventing it from cascading down your siding and pooling at your foundation.
  • Downspouts: These vertical pipes carry water from the gutters safely to the ground. Proper placement is key to directing water away from your home’s base, preventing basement flooding and structural issues.
  • Elbows: These angled pieces are crucial for navigation. They connect gutters to downspouts and direct water away from the foundation at the bottom.
  • Hangers & Fasteners: The unsung heroes that secure your gutters to the fascia board. Strong hangers are vital to support the weight of water and debris, preventing sagging.
  • Miters (Corners): These connect gutter sections at corners, ensuring a continuous, leak-proof flow. A well-installed miter is precisely cut and sealed.
  • End Caps: These seal the ends of gutter runs, preventing water from spilling out and forcing it toward the downspouts.
  • Splash Blocks: Placed under the downspout, these disperse water, preventing soil erosion right next to your foundation.

Each part is vital. A failure in any one component—a leaky miter, a clogged downspout, or a sagging gutter—can compromise the entire system’s ability to protect your home. How do gutters protect your home?

Material Matters: Choosing Between Vinyl, Aluminum, Steel, and More

When searching for rain gutter parts near me, the material is a key decision. Each option offers a different balance of durability, cost, and aesthetics, especially considering Utah’s climate.

At M&M Gutters & Exteriors, we’ve worked with all materials and can help you choose based on your budget and home style. Rain gutter materials guide

The Most Common Gutter Materials

  • Aluminum Gutters: The most popular choice (about 70% of homes), aluminum is lightweight, rust-proof, affordable, and comes in many colors. It’s ideal for seamless installations and lasts 30-50 years.
  • Vinyl Gutters (PVC): A budget-friendly DIY option that won’t rust. However, vinyl can crack in extreme temperatures and fade over time, with a lifespan of 20-25 years.
  • Steel Gutters: Known for strength, galvanized or stainless steel gutters withstand heavy snow and impacts. Galvanized steel can eventually rust, while stainless is highly resistant but more expensive.
  • Copper Gutters: The premium choice for beauty and longevity. Copper develops a unique patina, never rusts, and can last over 100 years, adding significant value to a home.

Vinyl vs Aluminum Gutters Which One Is Best?

Comparing Gutter Material Pros and Cons

To help you visualize the differences, here’s a quick comparison:

MaterialAverage LifespanCost (Relative)ProsCons
Aluminum30-50 yearsMediumLightweight, rust-proof, many colors, great for seamless, durable.Can dent easily, may warp if not installed properly.
Vinyl20-25 yearsLowInexpensive, easy DIY installation, won’t rust.Less durable, prone to cracking in extreme temps, can sag/fade, limited colors.
Galvanized Steel20-30 yearsMedium-HighVery strong, good for heavy snow/ice.Heavier, can rust if coating is scratched, requires professional installation.
Stainless Steel50+ yearsHighExtremely durable, rust-proof, sleek modern look.Very expensive, heavy, requires professional installation.
Copper50-100+ yearsVery HighExceptional durability, beautiful patina, no rust, boosts home value.Very expensive, requires specialized installation.

When considering which material is best for your home in Utah, we factor in everything from average snowfall to your home’s architectural style. Which kind of rain gutter is best for you and your home?

Gutter Styles and Recognizing Signs of Failure

Beyond material, gutter style affects performance and the specific rain gutter parts near me you’ll need. The main choices are seamless vs. sectional and K-style vs. half-round.

Seamless vs. Sectional:

  • Sectional Gutters: Found at hardware stores in pre-cut lengths (e.g., 10-foot). They are joined with connectors, creating seams that can leak and snag debris.
  • Seamless Gutters: Custom-made on-site to fit your home’s exact dimensions. With seams only at corners, they drastically reduce leak risks and are our preferred method at M&M Gutters & Exteriors. What are seamless rain gutters?

K-Style vs. Half-Round:

  • K-Style Gutters: The most common profile, resembling crown molding. They hold more water than half-round gutters of the same width.
  • Half-Round Gutters: Semicircular gutters with a classic look, often used on historic homes. Their smooth interior helps prevent debris buildup.

The style you choose dictates the compatible elbows, miters, and hangers. What types of rain gutters are there?

Common Signs of Damaged Gutter Parts

Proactively identifying wear and tear can save you from costly repairs. Look for these red flags:

  • Cracks or Splits: Visible fissures, especially at seams, will lead to leaks.
  • Peeling Paint: Peeling paint on the fascia board behind the gutter indicates water is overflowing or leaking.
  • Rust Spots: On metal gutters (except copper), rust signals corrosion and impending failure.
  • Sagging or Pulling Away: Gutters pulling away from the house indicate failing hangers or rotted fascia, often due to clogs.
  • Water Marks on Fascia: Dark stains or mildew under the gutters are clear signs of leaks.
  • Foundation Erosion: Trenches or washed-out landscaping below show water isn’t being diverted properly. This is a critical issue that can lead to serious structural problems. According to FEMA, water is a primary cause of foundation problems.
  • Basement Flooding: A damp or flooded basement is a sure sign your gutter system is failing.

Don’t ignore these warnings! Early action prevents minor issues from becoming major renovations. 5 Signs Your Home Needs a New Gutter System

The Role of Soffit and Fascia

The fascia is the board your gutters mount to, and the soffit is the underside of the roof’s overhang. If gutters overflow, the fascia can rot, weakening the gutter’s attachment. Signs of rot include peeling paint, soft spots, or crumbling wood. Soffit is key for attic ventilation, and damage there can also signal moisture problems. If you see soffit or fascia damage, a full gutter inspection is wise. How to determine if you need a soffit and fascia replacement

Your Local Search: Where to Find Rain Gutter Parts Near Me

When you need to find rain gutter parts near me in the Salt Lake City area, you have two main paths: DIY or professional. Your choice depends on the project’s scope and your comfort level.

Finding DIY Rain Gutter Parts Near Me

For the DIYer, standard parts are available at local hardware stores. You’ll find sectional aluminum or vinyl gutters in 10-foot or 20-foot lengths, plus the necessary downspouts, elbows, and hangers.

Pros of DIY parts:

  • Immediate availability: Pick up parts the same day.
  • Lower upfront cost: Sectional components are generally cheaper.
  • Accessibility: Widely available in Salt Lake, Utah, and Davis counties.

Cons of DIY parts:

  • Limited selection: Fewer choices for colors, materials (like copper), or custom lengths.
  • More seams: Sectional gutters have many seams, which are potential leak points.
  • Durability issues: Vinyl may crack in Utah’s temperature extremes.

DIY is a viable option for minor repairs on sectional systems. For extensive damage or the long-term benefits of a seamless system, professional help is the better route.

Sourcing Professional-Grade Rain Gutter Parts Near Me

For homeowners in Salt Lake City and surrounding areas like Summit, Tooele, and Weber counties, M&M Gutters & Exteriors is your trusted expert for professional-grade rain gutter parts near me.

Working with us provides key advantages:

  • Access to Seamless Gutters: We custom-fabricate seamless gutters on-site to fit your home perfectly, minimizing leaks and creating a clean look.
  • Wide Material Selection: We offer durable materials like copper and heavy-gauge steel that standard stores don’t carry.
  • Custom Solutions: With 30+ years of experience and 3D visualization via HOVER, we design systems custom to your home and Utah’s climate.
  • Expert Installation: Our team ensures correct slope, secure fastening, and watertight seals, preventing future problems.

While DIY can seem cheaper, professional installation with quality parts is a smarter investment that saves you from costly repairs down the road. Why you shouldn’t install your rain gutters yourself

Beyond the Parts: Installation, Maintenance, and Protection

Having the right rain gutter parts near me is just the start. Proper installation and maintenance are what make a gutter system truly effective at protecting your home.

Correct installation is paramount. Even the best parts will fail if installed with the wrong slope or insecure fasteners, leading to leaks and water damage. After installation, regular maintenance is key. This involves cleaning, inspections, and considering protective additions like gutter guards.

The Importance of Gutter Guards

Gutter guards (or leaf protection systems) cover your gutters to keep debris out while letting water in. They are a smart investment, especially in Utah’s leafy neighborhoods.

Key benefits include:

  • Preventing Clogs: They block leaves, twigs, and pine needles, ensuring water flows freely.
  • Reducing Maintenance: They drastically cut down on the need for frequent, dangerous gutter cleaning. The importance of cleaning your rain gutters
  • Extending Gutter Life: By preventing clogs and standing water, they reduce weight and corrosion.
  • Deterring Pests & Ice Dams: They stop pests from nesting and can help prevent ice dams by maintaining proper drainage.
  • Cost-Benefit: An installation costing between $500 and $2,000 can prevent thousands in water damage repairs.

Maintenance Best Practices

A little proactive care goes a long way.

  • Regular Cleaning: Clean gutters at least twice a year (late spring and fall). With guards, a visual check and clearing of surface debris is usually enough.
  • Inspect for Damage: While cleaning, look for cracks, rust, loose hangers, or gaps.
  • Check the Slope: Ensure a slight slope (about 1/4 inch per 10 feet) toward the downspouts to prevent standing water.
  • Clear Downspouts: Make sure downspouts are clear and that water is directed away from the foundation with splash blocks or extensions.
  • Post-Winter Check: After snow melts, inspect for any damage from ice or heavy snow loads. Rain Gutters Spring Cleaning After Winter

Consistent maintenance saves you from costly surprises. Helpful tips for maintaining your gutter system

Conclusion: Assembling Your Perfect Gutter Solution

We’ve journeyed through the essential components of a rain gutter system, from the main troughs and downspouts to the crucial connectors like elbows, miters, and end caps. We’ve explored the diverse materials available—vinyl, aluminum, steel, and copper—each with its own strengths and weaknesses, suitable for different budgets and aesthetic preferences in Salt Lake City and across Northern Utah. We’ve also highlighted the critical role of proper installation, the benefits of gutter guards, and the importance of ongoing maintenance to protect your home from the often-underestimated threat of water damage.

The value of a functional gutter system cannot be overstated. It’s not just about aesthetics; it’s about safeguarding your home’s foundation, siding, landscaping, and overall structural integrity. A well-maintained system prevents expensive repairs, keeps your basement dry, and even deters pests.

Whether you’re hunting for specific rain gutter parts near me for a small repair or considering a complete system overhaul, understanding these components empowers you to make informed decisions. While local hardware stores can be a good source for basic, sectional parts, for professional-grade, seamless, or specialized solutions, working with a local expert like M&M Gutters & Exteriors offers unparalleled benefits. Our 30+ years of experience in Salt Lake City, Utah, and surrounding counties mean we understand the unique challenges our local climate presents.

For a complete, professional solution that ensures your home is protected, consider expert installation from a team that knows gutters inside and out. We’re here to help you protect your most valuable asset. Services: Rain Gutters Installation

You may submit your credit card information online or over the phone when you sign up for our services. We process payments through E online data. Use of Personal Information

Security Information

Changes to This Privacy Policy

content:
EXTERIOR SIDING CONTRACTORS IN SALT LAKE CITY

Siding Is One Of The Best Ways To Improve Your Home And Its Energy Efficiency

As a protective shell for your house, siding provides protection from the harsh elements of Utah and keeps the indoors dry and comfortable. There are many different types of siding, from classic vinyl to cedar. Each type offers unique benefits, whether you’re looking for durability, low maintenance, or aesthetic appeal, which is why you should work with professionals to choose the type that best suits your needs.

At M&M Gutters & Exteriors, we understand that choosing the right siding is an important decision that affects your home’s look and functionality. Our expert exterior siding contractors in Salt Lake City are dedicated to treating your home with the same care and consideration they would their own. We take pride in offering personalized consultations to help you feel comfortable in your decision as you build or renovate your home. Our sales team will take the time you need to make such a critical decision.

Ready to transform your home’s exterior? Contact us today for a free consultation, and let our experienced sales team guide you through the process of selecting exterior siding in Salt Lake City.

Exterior Siding Installation Services

Using various materials and styles, our experienced exterior siding contractors in Salt Lake City can quickly and efficiently install siding that fits your home’s needs and aesthetic. Proper siding that is well-suited to your house will improve your home’s energy efficiency and curb appeal.

Our installation process begins with a thorough assessment of your home’s structure and your personal preferences. We offer a wide range of siding options, including Prodigy, Charter Oak, Odyssey, Conquest, and more. Our team will guide you through the selection process to help you understand the pros and cons of each type of siding and choose the right type for you.

Once you’ve chosen your ideal siding, our skilled contractors with over 30 years of combined experience will use advanced techniques to install your siding. We pay careful attention to details like proper insulation, ventilation, and moisture barriers to maximize your siding’s performance and longevity. Our goal is to install durable siding that will protect your home from the elements, especially from the rough winters of Salt Lake City, UT.

Siding Repair Services

If severe weather or other issues have broken your home’s siding, our team can inspect the damage to help you determine the best course of action. Our contractors use high-quality materials, state-of-the-art tools, and proven techniques to ensure our repairs contribute to the lifespan and beauty of your home.

Our repair process starts with a comprehensive inspection to assess the extent of the damage. We look beyond surface-level issues to identify any underlying problems that could compromise your siding’s integrity. This thorough approach allows us to provide an accurate diagnosis and cost-effective solutions.

Whether replacing a few damaged panels, addressing water damage, or fixing issues with insulation, our team has the expertise to handle all kinds of siding repairs. We always aim to match the existing siding seamlessly so the repairs are virtually invisible. If your siding has suffered extensive damage, we can advise on partial or full siding replacement options to protect your home and your budget.

A Better-Looking Home Starts with the Right Contractor

See what your Salt Lake Valley homeowners are saying about our exterior siding work.

Find more reviews from happy homeowners on:

How Much Does Siding Cost in Salt Lake City?

There’s no way around it — one of the biggest factors in choosing a siding contractor in Salt Lake City is cost. There’s no way around it. The price of your project will depend on several factors, including the material you choose and the size of your home. Here’s a quick look at options to help you set a budget for your project:

Vinyl siding

$6–$7 per square foot for basic siding or $8–$9 for premium siding

For an average 2,500-square-foot home in Salt Lake City, you can expect to invest:

$15,000–$22,500

Fiber cement siding

$9–$11 per square foot

For an average 2,500-square-foot home in Salt Lake City, you can expect to invest:

$22,500–$27,500

Cedar siding

$16–$18 per square foot

For an average 2,500-square-foot home in Salt Lake City, you can expect to invest:

$40,000–$45,000

Our Process

With so many siding contractors in Salt Lake City, it can be difficult to know whom to trust. At M&M Gutters & Exteriors, we take every exterior siding project very seriously, from start to finish. Here’s what you can expect when you hire us to handle your Salt Lake City exterior siding project.

1. Assess and Remove Existing Siding

The very first step is to conduct a thorough evaluation of your home’s current state. Our experienced contractors in Salt Lake City will carefully remove the existing siding, taking precautions to protect windows, doors, and landscaping. This allows us to uncover any hidden issues and prepare a clean slate for your new siding.

2. Evaluate the Sheathing

Once the old siding is removed, we conduct a comprehensive inspection of your home’s sheathing and framework. This step identifies any moisture damage, insect infestation, or structural issues that may have been concealed. Addressing these problems early enables us to prevent any future complications with your new siding, which could be costly.

3. Preparing the Exterior

Before installing new siding, we focus on creating an ideal surface. This may involve repairs or replacing damaged sheathing, upgrading insulation, and installing a weather-resistant barrier, depending on the status of your home.

4. Creating Proper Ventilation and Moisture Control

Proper airflow and moisture management help keep your siding safe and sturdy for a long time. We implement advanced techniques to confirm there’s adequate ventilation and install appropriate moisture barriers. This step helps prevent issues like mold growth and premature deterioration of your new siding.

5. Installation of New Siding

With a solid foundation in place, our skilled exterior siding technicians begin installing your chosen siding. Whether it’s vinyl, fiber cement, or another material, we adhere to manufacturer specifications and industry best practices.

6. Clean Up

As the installation process nears completion, we focus on the fine details that make a big difference. We’ll apply caulk where necessary, painting or touching up exposed nail heads and confirming that all trim pieces are perfectly aligned.

Our Work in Salt Lake City

Want to see exactly what your home could look like with some exterior siding work from M&M Gutters & Exteriors? Take a look at some of our siding installations and siding repairs in Salt Lake City:

Different Grades of Siding

There are many kinds of siding, each with its own pros and cons. Here’s a quick breakdown of what you can expect from some of the top types of siding in Salt Lake City and whom they might be good for.

Prodigy Siding

This siding grade stands out for its innovative design featuring a built-in insulation system. Prodigy siding provides superior impact resistance, making it an excellent choice for areas prone to severe weather, like Salt Lake City. Homeowners looking for a blend of comfort and durability tend to go for this type of siding.

      • RigidLock Locking Feature
      • Premium 5″, 6″ and 7″ Exposure Widths
      • 1-1/2″ Precisely Contoured Insulation
      • Subtle, Finely Milled Grain Finish
      • Lifetime, Transferable Warranty (manufacturers)

      • Panel Thickness: 1.5″ (nominal)

Charter Oak Siding

For those who love the classic look of wood without the maintenance hassles, Charter Oak siding is the answer. Its authentic wood-grain appearance is nearly indistinguishable from real wood. Thanks to the patented TriBeam design, this siding grading is exceptionally rigid and can withstand winds without losing its shape.

      • Choice of Natural Oak Grain or Matte Finish

Odyssey siding offers a perfect blend of beauty and performance with its double-thick nail hem and advanced locking system. Its unique design allows for expansion and contraction so that there’s always a tight fit in all weather conditions — all while maintaining a smooth, flat appearance.

Conquest Siding

Strength doesn’t have to come at a premium price. Conquest siding proves this with its rolled-over nail hem, providing extra strength and wind resistance at a cost-effective price point. It’s an ideal choice for budget-conscious homeowners who refuse to compromise on quality.

      • Texture: Cedar Grain

Board and Batten Siding

You can add depth and character to your home’s exterior with the distinctive vertical design of board and batten siding. Wide boards alternating with narrow battens create a visually captivating pattern that can evoke either rustic charm or modern sophistication, depending on your color and finish choices.

      • Subtle Cedar Finish
      • Low-Gloss Finish for the look of Freshly Painted Wood
      • Lifetime, Transferable Warranty

      • Texture: Finely Milled Cedar

Ovation Siding

Ovation siding stands out thanks to its thickness and deep wood grain patterns. Its innovative design includes a hidden seam, creating a cleaner look and improved weather resistance. Homeowners seeking a perfect balance of durability and aesthetics need to look no further.

      • Our Exclusive Snap+Lock+Hold Locking System Keeps Panels in Place, Even During High Winds

Carved Wood Siding

Nothing quite compares to the luxurious appeal of hand-carved details on real wood. Each piece of carved wood siding features distinctive variations and textures of genuine wood, offering an unparalleled level of craftsmanship and natural beauty.

      • Two Attractive Finishes, Smooth or Woodgrain
      • Mimics the Beauty of Real Wood

Quest Siding

If you’re looking for siding that’s easy to install and maintain, then Quest siding is for you. Its locking system enables a secure fit, while its durable construction resists common issues like fading, cracking, and peeling, promising long-lasting beauty with minimal maintenance.

Choosing the Right Exterior Siding

When you build or renovate a home, your choice of siding will be a major influence on your home’s look and energy efficiency. At M&M Gutters, we’ve been performing soffit roof repair and installing fascia for nearly 30 years, so you can trust that we’ll get the job done right every time.

What Are Soffit and Fascia?

Soffit and fascia are essential to your home’s exterior as they protect against moisture damage and other environmental factors. The soffit goes on the underside of your roof’s overhang to help ventilate your attic and prevent moisture buildup.

The fascia is the board that runs along the edge of your roof, connecting the roof to the walls of your home. It is designed to protect this edging area from weather damage while supporting your gutters.

It is crucial to have proper soffits and fascia on your home to prevent moisture problems like mold, rot, or even structural damage. And since soffits help with ventilation, not having them causes your heating and cooling systems to work harder to maintain comfortable temperatures, which could increase energy costs.

Choosing the Right Soffit and Fascia Materials

When it comes to fascia and soffit installation in Salt Lake City, you want to ensure you’re choosing the right materials for your project. Your options are:

Steel

  • Resistant to mold, mildew, and rot
  • Low maintenance and easy to clean
  • Energy efficient
  • Durable and long-lasting
  • Doesn’t warp or split like wood
  • Modern look and design

Wood

  • Natural and aesthetic appeal
  • Can be stained or painted to match your home’s design
  • Available in various wood species
  • Durable and long-lasting if properly maintained
  • Provides good insulation and energy efficiency

PVC

  • Resistant to mold, mildew, and rot
  • Resistant to peeling, fading, or chipping
  • Does not need to be painted
  • Easy to install
  • Available in various colors and styles

Fiber cement

  • Provides excellent protection and ventilation
  • Resistant to warping or splitting like wood
  • Low maintenance
  • Does not need to be painted
  • Resistant to moisture and water damage

Aluminum

  • Lightweight
  • Non-combustible and fire-resistant
  • Resistant to peeling, fading, or chipping
  • Resistant to moisture and water damage
  • Durable and long-lasting

Different Grades of Soffit and Fascia

In addition to the different types of soffit and fascia, they also come in several grades.

    • Economy — This is the thinnest and least expensive option and is typically used in low-cost housing or temporary structures.
    • Standard — This is a mid-range option that balances cost and durability. It is typically used for residential structures and is designed to withstand moderate weather conditions.
    • Heavy-duty — This is the thickest and most durable option and is ideal for areas with harsh weather conditions.
    • Premium — This is the most expensive option but is highly durable and long-lasting. It is usually used for commercial buildings or high-end residential projects.

h1: Leaf Guards for Rain Gutters

Leaf Guards for Rain Gutters

Cleaning out your rain gutters is extremely important. Clogged gutters can cause damage to a home’s foundation and walls. Over time, this can cause the fascia boards and soffit to deteriorate and eventually rot. We offer several Utah leaf guard solutions to accommodate your home‘s specific needs.

The Best Gutter Guards For Your Home

Identifying the best leaf guards for your rain gutters can be an overwhelming task — but not if you know what to look for. Find out why M&M leaf guards and gutter installation are a smart choice for Utah homeowners.

What Do Gutter Guards Do?

Gutter guards are also referred to as leaf guards or gutter covers. They are installed over the top of your rain gutters, creating a barrier that blocks out debris while directing water away from your home. Ultimately, gutter guards prevent frustrating blockages that contribute to costly home water damage.

Gutter guards come in a couple of different varieties, including wire mesh leaf guards and aluminum screens — and the right one for you will depend mainly on the type of debris you get on your roof and your gutter system design.

What to Look for in Leaf Guards for Rain Gutters

When you’re trying to determine the right gutter for your house, compatibility and durability are two important factors to keep in mind. Do you have an asphalt, metal, tile, or flat roof? For example, asphalt shingles can be compatible with most gutter guard types, including mesh screens and solid covers, while tile roofs might only work with mesh screens that won’t shift around from the tile weight.

You also want your Utah leaf guards to last, so make sure to seek out high-quality products constructed from aluminum, stainless steel, or copper so your investment lasts.

Materials Used

M&M gutter guards are made of wire mesh and aluminum. We’ve chosen these materials because not only have they proven to be effective, but they’re also quite affordable and can withstand rough weather, extreme temperatures, and prolonged sun exposure. Aluminum and wire mesh leaf guards are also widely compatible with most gutter types and are relatively low maintenance. They’re even resistant to rust and corrosion and can last for years with occasional cleanings.

Cost

The prices of gutter guards often depend on the product type, material, size of your home, and how complex the installation will be. Remember that gutter guards are an investment, but they can prevent more expensive water damage to your home in the long term. M&M offers reliable quotes on leaf guard gutter installation, so there are never surprises at the cost of your new gutter guard system.

Wire mesh screen is a very economical solution to clogged rain gutters. It works very well in areas that have larger leaves. One big benefit of wire mesh leaf guards for rain gutters is the dome shape that keeps leaves from getting into the gutter. It also allows the wind to help clean the screens off.

Pros and Cons

Pros:

  • Cost-effective gutter guard option
  • Keeps out large debris
  • Reduces the need for frequent cleaning
  • Quick to install

Cons:

  • Smaller debris can still get through — i.e., pine needles, seeds, etc.
  • Less durable than alternative guard types

Gutter Rx Leaf Guard

Gutter Rx is an aluminum screen that lays flat in the gutters to give it an invisible look. It has small ridges that act as channels for the wind to blow the screen off and not allow build-up. These ridges also help by slowing water flow to ensure the water does not overflow the screen. Gutter Rx attaches to the front and back of the gutter, which reinforces the gutter system.

Cons:

The LeafX gutter guard is designed to withstand even the heaviest rain and snowfalls while preventing gutter clogs. It comes in high-flow and solid-cover designs to suit your needs. The nose-forward design uses surface tension to ensure ideal water flow, with rain following the curve of the hood into the gutter openings while leaves are shed off.

h1: RAIN GUTTERS INSTALLATION SERVICES IN SALT LAKE CITY
content:
RAIN GUTTERS INSTALLATION SERVICES IN SALT LAKE CITY

Your Property is Precious. Don’t Let Rainwater Sully It

Contact M&M Gutters and Exteriors for rain gutter installation services in Salt Lake City and protect your investment.

Why Do You Need Rain Gutters?

Rain gutters capture water that collects on your roof and divert it from your property. You need rain gutters to:

Prevent foundation damage

Gutters ensure that the water collected from the roof is disposed of properly and efficiently and directed away from the foundation.

Prevent basement flooding

Without a gutter system, water can infiltrate your home and flood your basement or crawl space, resulting in costly damage of up to $6,241.

Protect fascia and soffit from Rotting

Fascia primarily serves to protect the underlying structure of a home from water damage while Soffits provide proper airflow and ventilation to the attic.

Prevent Driveway cracks

Gutters help by directing water away from the concrete slab, preventing excessive water from pooling around edges and causing the concrete to expand and contract unevenly, which is a major contributing factor to cracking.

Prevent landscape damage

By isolating the water to the downspouts, a good gutter system will prevent excessive water runoff that can erode soil, and disruption to the stability of the surrounding landscaping.

Prevent ice formation to doorsteps and walkways

Gutters over entryways and walkways ensure that water is redirected from both entrances and walkways, which then prevents unsafe ice build up in winter months.

Keep pests away

Gutters help by preventing the accumulation of standing water which is the prime breeding ground for insects like mosquitoes. A well-functioning gutter system reduces excess moisture around the house which deters many types of pests from inhabiting the area.

Rain Gutter Installation

Gutter installation is a sensitive task. Don’t leave it to just anyone — or you could end up with undesirable results. Hire us for professional rain gutter installation services in Salt Lake City. We have over three decades of experience installing rain gutters made from high-quality materials such as copper, aluminum, and steel.

One inspection now beats a season of water damage later.

Rain Gutter Repair

Gutter damage can result in costly foundation repairs of up to $7,921. If you wait until it’s too late, you might have to fork out thousands of dollars on foundation repairs. If your gutters are misaligned, sagging, or have cracks, you should act fast to prevent even more expensive repairs. Hire us for timely rain gutter repair in Salt Lake City to extend the lifespan of your gutters and protect your property.

Rain Gutter Cleaning

Gutters require routine maintenance and cleaning to keep them in good condition. If your gutters are clogged or overflowing, contact us to schedule gutter cleaning. We’ll thoroughly clean and flush them to ensure they work properly and divert water from your home. Professional gutter cleaning built for Utah weather, starting at $150.

Residential and Commercial Gutter Installation & Repair

There’s no one-size-fits-all gutter solution for all buildings. Whether you require residential or commercial gutter installation and repair, our team has the experience and expertise to handle various projects, big or small.

Leaf Protection Year Round

Gutters are prone to accumulating debris over time and may require frequent cleaning. Tired of scheduling regular clean-ups or cleaning out your gutter yourself? Our innovative roof leaf guards offer year-round protection, so you can bid farewell to the hassle of frequent gutter cleaning.

Utah Homeowners Trust M&M Gutters & Exteriors

See what your Salt Lake Valley neighbors are saying about our rain gutter installations.

Find more reviews from happy homeowners on:

Convinced? Let’s get to work.

Free yourself from the hassle of climbing up the ladder to clean or repair your gutter. Contact us today to get a free quote.

Types of Gutters

Rain gutters come in several varieties to suit different home sizes and roof types. Each style of gutter has unique benefits.

K-style gutters are typically the most common rain gutters in Utah and come in the standard 5-inch size and a larger 6-inch size. Half-round gutters have a more rounded profile that not only increases water flow but also adds elegance to the exterior design. Copper, which is known for its long-term durability, is also a sophisticated option. Lastly, commercial custom box gutters are usually found on commercial properties but can be made to the property owner’s unique specifications. We elaborate on each gutter type below.

K-Style Rain Gutters

K-style rain gutters somewhat resemble the letter K when viewed from the side.

K-style gutters are used in most homes in Utah. They’re called K-style gutters because they resemble the letter K when viewed from the side. These seamless gutter systems are an economical way to add value to your home while protecting it. M&M Gutters offers this K style in two sizes, 5′′ and 6′′, with 5′′ being standard on most residential homes. Homeowners can choose from aluminum, steel, galvanized, and copper.

Half-Round Gutters

Half-round gutters, shaped like a tube cut in half, carry water very effectively.

Half-round gutters add a classic and elegant look to most homes. These gutters have been around for centuries, and some consider them to be the superior gutter system. The rounded profile allows half-round gutters to increase the water flow out of the gutter — unlike the K-style, which will have residual water remaining. Half-round gutters are available in aluminum, steel, galvanized, and copper.

M&M Gutters has installed thousands of feet of half-round gutters on homes and many different historical sites throughout Utah.

Commercial Custom Box Gutters

Box gutters are made according to the specifications of the building and can be made in many different sizes and designs. This type of gutter is typically found on commercial buildings or older buildings. One of the most significant benefits of box gutters is that they can come in thicker metals than standard-formed gutters. The gutter size can also be much larger to capture all the water that comes off the roof. Box gutter systems can be formed to go entirely under the roofing system to ensure a sturdy installation.

To familiarize you with gutters, here are some basic gutter components.

Parts of a Gutter System

Gutter systems are made of several components that direct water away from your home and prevent damage to its structural integrity. Some of the primary features of a gutter system include the following:

Rain gutters

These are the parts that probably come to mind when you think about gutters; they’re the long, narrow channels that collect rainwater and span the edge of your roof.

Drop outlet

This component connects rain gutters to downspouts at the bottom of a gutter’s vertical section. It has a round or rectangular opening for the downspout to fit into.

Leaf screen

Also known as a leaf guard or gutter guard, this component keeps leaves and other debris from getting into the gutter system and creating blockages.

Inside corner

This pre-formed metal piece fits over the gutter's edge to connect two inner sections of the channel.

Elbows

These curved devices connect downspouts to gutters, allowing the water to change directions.

Bracket hanger

This device supports the weight of the gutter from within and is fastened to rafter tails or the fascia board.

Outside corner

Like the inside corner, the outside corner connects two outer gutter sections and is fastened in place with screws or rivets.

End caps

These seal the ends of the gutters to keep water from escaping.

Splash blocks

Spike and ferrule

This is a traditional mechanism for hanging gutters. The spike, a long, pointed metal rod, goes through the front of the gutter into the fascia board. The ferrule is a tube-like mechanism inserted into the back of the gutter for support to prevent a collapse around the spike.

Strap

This metal strip supports the weight of the gutter.

How Are Gutters Installed?

Slope Layout and Chalk Line

Rain gutters need to be angled precisely to direct water toward the downspouts. Once the correct slope is determined, we’ll mark a chalk line to ensure proper installation.

Cut and Fabricate the Gutter

For professional roof heat cable installation in Salt Lake City, contact the roofing experts at M&M Gutters.

What Are Heating Cables?

A heat cable for a roof is an electrical wire that can be heated up during snowfall to prevent snow and ice from accumulating on the edges of your roof.

Different Types of Heat Cables

You can get two types of heating cables for your roof: self-regulating and constant wattage.

Self-regulating heat cables produce heat based on the temperature around them. This means that if one section is warmer than another, the first section of the cable won’t heat up as much as the cooler section because it doesn’t need to.

On the other hand, constant-wattage heating cables produce consistent, stable heat throughout the entire cable to ensure it is equally distributed along the line.

During your roof heat cable installation in Salt Lake City, our team can help you decide which type of heating cable is best for your home and needs.

Benefits of Heat Cables

There are several benefits of adding a heat cable to your roof. Heat cables are installed in a zigzag pattern throughout the lower colder section of the roof to prevent the water from freezing and leading to further issues. One of the main benefits of doing roof heat cable installation in Salt Lake City is listed below.

How Heat Cables Prevent Ice Dams and Protect the Home

The part of your roof that extends out from the edge is typically colder than the rest of the roof. This means that when the upper section warms up due to your home heating system, snow will melt and run down toward the cooler area by your gutters. Once this water hits the colder section, it can refreeze, causing problems with frozen pipes, water damage, and even ice dams.

Preventing Ice Dams and Damage to Roofing Systems

If there are several days worth of snow melting and refreezing on your roof, it can slowly build up into an ice dam. This blockage is problematic, as the ice buildup can get under shingles and push them up, which ruins the shingles and allows water to get under them and into your attic space.

Using heating cables to prevent ice dams is helpful because it only targets the problematic areas, so you won’t have to worry about heating your entire roof or the extra associated costs. Additionally, ice dams contribute to icicles, which are injury hazards for you and your loved ones. So getting heat cables for your roof also helps keep you safer during the winter months.

Evaluate the Sheathing

With the siding removed, we examine the sheathing and framework underneath. If we find moisture damage or deterioration, we make the necessary repairs and add a weather-resistant barrier to give your new siding a strong, dry base.

Prepare the Exterior

Before installation, we repair structural imperfections, upgrade insulation if needed, and apply protective layers. This ensures a smooth, even surface that helps your new siding perform its best.

Create Proper Ventilation and Moisture Control

Moisture is a home’s worst enemy. We install drainage systems, flashing, and ventilation solutions that allow air to circulate while keeping water out. This step is critical for preventing mold, mildew, and premature wear.

Install New Siding

Once the groundwork is laid, our team installs your chosen stucco, stone, or blended siding. We follow a meticulous step-by-step process to ensure every panel and section is secure, level, and aligned, resulting in a durable exterior with a seamless finish.

Clean Up

content:
SALT LAKE CITY
FULL HOME WINDOW REPLACEMENT

Are rising energy bills and drafty rooms making your home feel uncomfortable? Your windows may be to blame. As Salt Lake City’s leading full-home window replacement contractor, we’re here to help you enjoy a more beautiful, comfortable, and energy-efficient home.

Don’t settle for outdated windows. Let our full home window replacement experts get the job done right — and fast. Contact M&M Gutters today!

Replace Your Windows For Better Home Efficiency

Windows are designed to keep weather elements out and your energy bills low. Unfortunately, old windows struggle to do either job effectively. Whether they’re dirty, damaged, or outdated, it’s no surprise that “full-home window replacement in Salt Lake City” is a popular search topic for homeowners.

Benefits of Full-Home Window Replacement

Full-home window replacement from M&M Gutters offers several benefits for homeowners, including:

Improved Energy Efficiency

Most older windows are single-pane and have poor insulation due to their thin materials. With new windows, you can opt for multiple glass panes and thicker frames to minimize airflow around the perimeter and improve insulation.

Increased home value

New windows enhance the value of your home and are an attractive feature for homebuyers.

Enhanced Curb Appeal

If you want to spruce up your home’s exterior, home window replacement in Salt Lake City is an excellent way to improve your curb appeal.

Better noise control

Even if you don’t live on a noisy street, chances are you still prefer a little peace and quiet. Modern windows are constructed with multiple panes of glass to reduce outside noise and maintain a peaceful home environment.

Improved home security

Older windows have thinner frames and typically lack strong locking mechanisms compared to newer windows. When you work with our full-home window replacement contractors in Salt Lake City, you get beautiful new windows that better protect your home.

Our Window Services

When it comes to full-home window replacement and exteriors , Utah has no better experts than M&M Gutters & Exteriors. Here are a few of the services we offer.

New/Replacement Windows

Replace your outdated and damaged windows from a selection of attractive and energy-efficient styles.

Sliding Glass Doors

Let the light in and improve movement through your home with beautiful, durable glass sliding doors.

Vinyl Siding Installation

Protect your home from the elements while improving its curb appeal with new vinyl siding.

Window Installation

Windows are a necessary part of our homes, but most people don’t give them much thought on a daily basis. However, full-window installation can completely change your home’s look and feel, which is why we love completing full-home window replacement installations in Salt Lake City.

Choose Your Dream Windows

When replacing the windows in your Salt Lake City home, you have several different types to choose from. While we can install almost any window you’re looking for, here are some of our most popular installations.

Single-Hung
Single-hung windows are one of the most popular options we install. These windows feature two pieces, one on top, which is stationary, and one on the bottom, which moves up and down. Typically, single-hung windows are more cost-effective and energy-efficient. Double-Hung
Double-hung windows function the same as their single counterparts. The only difference is that the window’s top and bottom move instead of just the bottom. These windows are easier to clean, have more design options, and allow for more ventilation throughout your home. Casement
Casement windows, often called crank windows, have hinges on one side and open to the left or right. These windows offer a unique design detail, have excellent airflow, and generally receive high security ratings. Sliding
Sliding windows are the most common option for any new build or replacement window installation in Salt Lake City. These windows move along a top and bottom track to slide open or closed. These windows are easy to clean, offer lots of natural light, and have a streamlined, simple design. Bay Windows
Bay windows are generally a three-sectioned piece made up of one larger window in the middle and two smaller ones on the sides, all of which are typically single-hung windows. These windows have a beautiful, functional design inside and out, can improve resale value based on their look, and let in lots of natural light thanks to multiple windows.

Window Materials Designed to Match Your Home’s Style

At M&M Gutters, we offer a variety of window materials to blend seamlessly with your home’s style. Whether you prefer a classic, modern, or custom aesthetic, we’ll help you find the perfect fit.

Vinyl Windows

Vinyl windows are ideal if you’re looking for an affordable and low-maintenance option. They come in various colors and are extremely well insulated to keep your home comfortable all year round.

Wood Windows

Wood windows bring natural warmth and charm to your home. They’re well-insulated and can easily be painted or stained to match the style of your home.

Fiberglass Windows

Fiberglass windows are energy-efficient and give your home a sleek, modern look. These frames are also resistant to cracking and warping in extreme weather conditions and can be painted a variety of colors.

Energy-Efficient Glass Options

Lower your energy bill with energy-efficient glass options, such as Low-E coatings and double- or triple-pane glass.

Window Frame Colors & Finishes

Whether you prefer a subtle blend or a standout accent color, we offer a range of color finishes to complement your style.

Full-Home Window Replacement Cost Factors

The cost of a full-home window replacement from M&M Gutters varies depending on several factors. Understanding these cost factors will help you make the most informed decision for your home and budget.

Material Costs

Window materials, such as vinyl, wood, and fiberglass, all have different prices. If you prefer a more affordable option, vinyl is the best choice. If you’re looking for a more premium option, wood and fiberglass are worth the higher cost.

Installation Costs

The cost of a professional window installation is determined by:

  • The number of windows
  • The size of the windows
  • The complexity of the installation
  • The structure of your home

Energy Savings ROI

If you buy energy-efficient windows with features like Low-E glass and gas fills, you can enjoy long-term savings on your energy bills.

Available Rebates & Tax Credits

If you decide to buy energy-efficient windows, you may be eligible for rebates or federal tax credits, which can help increase your overall savings.

How to Choose the Right Windows for Your Home

Unsure of what type of windows to choose for your home? Here are a few factors to consider that will help you decide.

Climate Considerations for Utah

Utah’s climate brings hot summers and cold, snowy winters. Look for windows with strong insulation and weather resistance to keep you comfortable throughout the year.

Energy Efficiency Ratings Explained

Look for energy ratings, such as U-factor and ENERGY STAR, to save on your heating and cooling bills. The lower the U-factor, the better the insulation.

Style & Architecture Matching

Find windows to make the look and feel of your home. Whether you have a traditional design or a modern build, the right window style will enhance your curb appeal.

Security Features

Protect you and your loved ones with windows featuring strong security features, such as reinforced locks and impact-resistant glass.

Fast, High-Quality Window Installation From Your Trusted Local Experts

Replacing old single-pane windows or repairing broken or damaged windows is one of the best ways to make your home more energy-efficient, comfortable, and secure.

Our Window Replacement Process

When you’re ready for a full-home window replacement, our team is here to help you every step of the way.

We’ll start with an initial consultation to discuss your window replacement needs and budget before measuring your existing window openings.

Measure & Manufacture

Once your windows arrive, we’ll work quickly and accurately to get them installed so you can get back to relaxing at home right away.

Customer Care

Your total satisfaction is our top priority before, during, and after installation. Whatever your questions, comments, or concerns, it’s our pleasure to work through them with you.

Why Choose M&M Gutters for Full-Home Window Replacement?

With nearly 30 years of experience improving people’s homes, M&M Gutters has earned a reputation as one of Utah’s best home service providers. Our work with windows is second to none, ensuring top-tier protection, aesthetics, and energy efficiency when you choose the experts at M&M Gutters & Exteriors.

No Payments and 0% Interest for 24 Months

That’s why we offer no payments and 0% interest for two years on approved credit (OAC) through Upgrade, which makes it easier for you to enjoy new windows now and pay later without added costs. This means you can improve your home’s energy efficiency, curb appeal, and property value without worrying about upfront payments or accumulating interest.

In addition to Upgrade, we also partner with Sunlight Financial to provide further financing solutions for your unique needs. Whether you’re looking for extended payment terms or flexible monthly options, we have a plan that works for you. Take advantage of these financing offers and start your window replacement project today with the peace of mind that comes from hassle-free payment options.

Rest Easy Knowing Your Windows Are Taken Care Of

At M&M Gutters, we’ll quickly and correctly remove and replace your problem windows. We can also repair various problems, including damaged casings, broken rails, and glass replacement. Whatever your window concerns may be, M&M Gutters’ home window replacement is the perfect choice for you.

Frequently Asked Questions

Process & Technical Questions

What is a full-home window replacement?

What’s the difference between full-frame and insert replacement?

A full-frame replacement is placed without your existing frame, whereas a window insert replacement fits a window into your existing frame. If your window frame is in good condition, you’ll most likely only need a window insert replacement.

How long does window installation take?

The timeframe for a window installation depends on the type and number of windows you’re looking to replace in your home. Our professional installers can give you a more accurate timeframe for either a full or insert window replacement.

Maintenance & Benefits of Full-Home Window Replacement

What are the signs I need new windows?

You may need new windows if:

    • You notice faded furniture
    • Your window frame is cracked or rotted
    • You have trouble opening and closing windows
    • You receive higher energy bills
    • You see condensation between the glass panes
    • You feel a draft coming from the windows
How much can I save on energy bills with new windows?

You can save up to 7-15% each year on heating and cooling costs by replacing your old windows with new ones. With M&M Gutters, you have a variety of options to choose from, ensuring your home remains properly insulated and comfortable throughout the year.

What warranty coverage is included?

The warranty coverage for a full window replacement includes protection against window seal failure and defects. With M&M Gutters, we’ll review the details of what’s covered and how long your coverage lasts to ensure your investment is protected.

Seasonal Maintenance and Cleaning Tips

You should care for your windows each season by:

    • Checking for signs of moisture around the frame
    • Using only soap and water to wash your windows
    • Removing dirt and debris from any weep holes in the exterior
    • Lubricating moving parts to avoid squeaky windows
